Jerry Jones Backs 'Young Coach' Christian Parker After Cowboys’ Defense Collapses
content: Jerry Jones isn’t ready to give up on Christian Parker leading the Cowboys defense. The Dallas Cowboys owner defended his first-year defensive coordinator Sunday night after the defense was torched in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium, pointing to Parker’s inexperience as a play-caller. "He’s a young coach. It’s his first year of coordinating and basically calling the plays," Jones told reporters. "I’ve been with teams that had some pretty good coordinators on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls." Sunday’s performance was the low point of a rough first season for Parker. The 49ers piled up 584 yards of offense, the most allowed by any team in a game this season and the most Dallas has ever surrendered at home. Christian McCaffrey sealed the win with a 66-yard touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter, just as the Cowboys got back into the game. Dallas has now allowed 102 points over its last three games. The decisive play came with veteran pass rusher Von Miller in coverage on McCaffrey, a matchup that drew plenty of criticism. Jones, though, put a positive spin on it. "He was closer than when they broke the other two big ones," Jones told reporters. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was far more blunt about what went wrong. He said the Cowboys did some good things in the first half against a very good 49ers offense, but that the defense fell apart after the break. "Very disappointed, very frustrated," Schottenheimer said. "What got us in the second half was the tackling, or the lack of tackling, and you got to get guys on the ground. And yeah, they’re good players, but at the end of the day, we tackled like s--- in the second half." Dallas hired Parker in January after the defense struggled throughout the 2025 season, and the team invested heavily on that side of the ball in the offseason. But the results haven’t followed, and the loss dropped the Cowboys to 4-6. With seven games left and the Cowboys two games under .500, Jones’ patience with his young coordinator could run out quickly if the defense doesn’t turn things around.

title: Overreaction Monday: Brock Purdy Is The MVP? Patriots Bound To Miss Playoffs?
content: Week 10 certainly wasn't your typical NFL Sunday. The day started in Germany, where two star players suffered potential season-altering injuries on the same play in the Detroit Lions' victory over the New England Patriots. It continued with a Super Bowl contender getting a much-needed performance from their new quarterback, as Kirk Cousins looked ready to carry the Minnesota Vikings into the postseason with their dominant win against the Green Bay Packers. Later in the day, the San Francisco 49ers outscored the Dallas Cowboys in arguably the best display of offensive football this season. In primetime, the Cincinnati Bengals' star duo of Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase continued to make history, putting on a show in their victory against the Pittsburgh Steelers. And all of that fails to mention that the No. 1 overall pick from this year's draft, Fernando Mendoza, made his first NFL start, and Patrick Mahomes might have had his best game in years on Sunday. So, what's real and what's fake from an extraordinary Sunday? Let's overreact to Week 10. Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers shredded the Dallas Cowboys' defense for 548 total yards in a 46-40 win on Sunday, which is the most yards the Cowboys have allowed in franchise history. The 49ers averaged 9.4 yards per play against the Cowboys, which was the most by any team in a game over the past two seasons, per FOX Sports Research. Purdy was a big part of that, completing 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. He upped his record to 4-0 against Dak Prescott, including the playoffs. The fifth-year quarterback has eight touchdown passes and zero interceptions in those games against the Cowboys. Also, San Francisco became the first team to record at least 370 passing yards and 200 rushing yards in the same game since 2023, when the Miami Dolphins did so in their 70-point effort against the Denver Broncos. Conclusion: Overreaction Purdy is playing at a high level and certainly in the conversation for league MVP this season, but Joe Burrow is still the leader in the clubhouse at this point. Burrow's 409-yard, four-touchdown day in the Cincinnati Bengals' dominating win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night should only increase his lead in the MVP race, as I crowned him my midseason MVP just a few days ago. Purdy does lead the league in passer rating (115.2) and has only thrown five interceptions this year. And unlike Burrow, Sunday showed that Purdy has one of the best running backs in the game to lean on. Christian McCaffrey had 161 receiving yards and two scores in his team’s dominant win, making history with his performance. If Purdy does want to be considered the MVP frontrunner, a showing against the Cowboys won't be enough to do that, as nearly every quarterback has torn Dallas' defense apart. But next week presents a strong opportunity for Purdy in the MVP race. He faces a stiff test when the 49ers take on the Minnesota Vikings and their top-ranked defense in Mexico City in Week 11. Speaking of Burrow, his Bengals made quick work of the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers in a battle for the top spot in the AFC North, winning 38-18. Pittsburgh’s defense had no answer for Burrow and his dynamic receivers, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Burrow finished with 409 passing yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. Most of that production came in the first half, too, as Burrow threw for 302 yards and three touchdowns in the opening 30 minutes. Burrow’s favorite target was Chase, who finished with 11 catches for 231 yards. It's Chase's third career game with 225-plus receiving yards, tying him with Calvin Johnson, Julio Jones and Jerry Rice for the most in NFL history, per FOX Sports Research. At 7-2, the Bengals own the top spot in the AFC North. Conclusion: Not An Overreaction The Buffalo Bills are tied with San Francisco for the best record in football at 8-1 and certainly have an argument for the best team in the league. But over the last month, no one has been as dominant as the Bengals. The Bengals have won their last five games, doing so with an average margin of victory of roughly 15 points (14.6). Of course, Burrow and the offense have been key to the Bengals' dominance as of late. Burrow has thrown for at least four touchdowns in each of the five games during the winning streak. He tied Peyton Manning’s record for the longest such streak since the NFL merger, as Manning did that back in 2004.  Burrow also leads the NFL with 20 games of at least 300 passing yards and at least three passing touchdowns since 2020. But Cincinnati's defense has stepped up during the winning streak, and it had another big performance on Sunday. The Bengals sacked Aaron Rodgers three times, and they also allowed just 40 yards in the first half. Rodgers didn't complete any of his first seven passes, giving him his most incompletions to start a game in his career. It was like he never left. With just a few days of practice, Kirk Cousins jumped right into head coach Kevin O’Connell’s offense and immediately added an explosive element to the Minnesota Vikings' passing game. Cousins finished 21 of 31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers. Specifically, Minnesota’s best offensive player, Justin Jefferson, was finally involved in the offense, finishing with nine catches for 74 yards on 13 targets. Minnesota’s 30 points were the most the Vikings have scored this season since a 39-22 win over the Packers in Week 1. The return of Cousins also allowed O’Connell to use more plays under center. They ran 34 offensive snaps (52.3%) after averaging 37% of their snaps under center through their first eight games, per Next Gen Stats. That ignited the running game for the Vikings. Minnesota rushed for 129 yards on 4.2 yards per carry on Sunday. That's the third-most rushing yards the Vikings have had in a game this season, and they did that after finishing with less than 100 rushing yards in each of their last two games (both losses). Conclusion: Overreaction As usual, Minnesota’s defense showed up and showed out. The Vikings forced four turnovers and sacked Jordan Love eight times, holding the Packers to 10 points. The last time the Vikings had at least eight sacks and four takeaways in a game was on October 22, 1989, against the Detroit Lions, according to FOX Sports Research. While Cousins’ play appears to be the missing piece for Minnesota, which has one of the dominant defenses in the league, the Vikings still play in the toughest division in the NFL. That means tough games await against NFC North foes, as they still have matchups against the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears. They also have a pair of tough non-divisional games, including next week against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City and at the New England Patriots on a Thursday night. Let’s see how Cousins performs against these teams destined for the postseason, and if he can stay healthy for the duration of the regular season. The New England Patriots' injury-ravaged roster might have reached its tipping point when quarterback Drake Maye left Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions after the opening drive with an ankle injury and did not return. Entering Sunday’s lopsided loss to the Lions, the Patriots had started a league-high 42 players this year due to injuries. Along with Maye, right tackle Morgan Moses suffered a knee injury but later returned to the game. No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown, who has missed six games with ankle and knee injuries, left the game in the second half with a hamstring injury. Brown had little impact when healthy, finishing with two catches for 27 yards on six targets. New England has lost two games in a row by an average of 21.5 points per contest. And at 5-5 with an injured franchise quarterback in Maye, the Patriots could be on the outside looking in when it comes to the postseason and getting back to the Super Bowl. Conclusion: Overreaction New England head coach Mike Vrabel’s specialty is defense, but that side of the football has been atrocious. The Patriots have allowed 300 passing yards in three of their last four games — all losses. The Patriots continued to surrender big plays against the Lions, allowing five passing plays of at least 20 yards. The Patriots gave up seven of those plays in a loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 9. Tommy DeVito did not look comfortable operating the offense in Maye’s absence, and New England’s offense will be impacted if the North Carolina product can’t return to action soon. Fortunately for the Patriots, they get a bye next week. But Vrabel has a lot of work to do during his team's off week. While things look bleak right now for New England, the teams chasing the Patriots are also struggling. The Cleveland Browns needed to come back from a 17-0 deficit to beat the three-win Houston Texans, and the Las Vegas Raiders lost for the sixth time in seven weeks on Sunday. Add to that the fact that New England gets the winless Los Angeles Chargers after the bye, and things could be looking up for the Patriots. Making his NFL debut against perhaps the best defense in the league, Fernando Mendoza more than held his own early on in the Las Vegas Raiders' loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Mendoza completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards and also had a rushing touchdown in the first half as the Raiders took an early 10-7 lead. Mendoza completed his first seven passes, joining Robert Griffin III and Derek Carr as the only rookie quarterbacks since 1991 to open their first NFL start with seven straight completions. However, Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald blitzed more in the second half, heating up the pass rush. The result was six sacks of Mendoza, including four in the fourth quarter, as the Seahawks finished with a 21-13 victory. Mendoza finished 17 of 29 for 143 yards, as he didn't throw a touchdown or an interception. Conclusion: Overreaction The Raiders were going to eventually move on from Kirk Cousins at some point this season so they could see what they have in Mendoza. And they received the perfect opportunity to do that, getting a third-round pick in return for trading him to the Minnesota Vikings, who could use the 38-year-old signal-caller to chase their Super Bowl window. Win-win. From talking to folks around the Raiders' organization, all indications were that Mendoza was more than ready to take the field. And he showed that in the first half. Las Vegas believes that Mendoza is a talented and mentally tough quarterback who can lead them to sustainable winning, something that hasn’t happened for a long time for the Raiders. Also, this team has lost six of their last seven games and they aren't built to compete for a deep postseason run at this point in their rebuild. It was time for Mendoza to take his rightful place as one of the leaders of this team so he could grow with the rest of the young core players. Patrick Mahomes got a new playmaker on offense this week and put him to good use. Josh Downs, whom the Kansas City Chiefs acquired at the trade deadline from the Indianapolis Colts, finished Sunday's 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons with four catches for 53 yards and a score. The addition of Downs gave Kansas City another pass catcher working out of the slot, making plays in the intermediate area of the field and opening things up down the field. Mahomes threw two deep touchdown passes in the win, which was his first game with multiple deep scores since 2021. Mahomes had thrown just one deep touchdown since the start of the 2025 season entering Week 10. Conclusion: Not An Overreaction Even with the team’s most explosive player, running back Kenneth Walker III (groin), out of this game with an injury, the Chiefs still dialed up big plays. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson posted 171 scrimmage yards and two scores, filling in for the Memphis native. Playing a week after spraining his right elbow, Mahomes had perhaps his best game of the season, throwing for 348 yards and five touchdowns. It’s the first time Mahomes has thrown five touchdowns in a game since September 2022, per FOX Sports Research. Even though Kansas City played without both starting offensive tackles and lost guard Trey Smith and tight end Travis Kelce during the game, Mahomes had his highest passing yards total of the season. And when Walker comes back healthy, he should be even more dangerous because defenses cannot totally key on him in the running and passing game, with the addition of Downs and the breakout game by Johnson.

title: Chiefs Have Found Perfect Ingredient To Make Another Run With Patrick Mahomes: Youth
content: MERCEDES-BENZ STADIUM (ATLANTA) — The fact that Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes Sunday in a 35-13 rout of the Falcons isn't in itself incredible. The Chiefs quarterback had done that six times before in his career, eight if you count playoff games. But consider the guys who caught those five touchdown passes, and it's an even more impressive feat: So, on two of those, Mahomes (who now has 359 career touchdowns) hurried to track down the game ball from a player's first NFL touchdown, to make sure he had a priceless keepsake, just as he still is proud of his first. "I mean, playing in the NFL is a dream," Mahomes explained after the Chiefs improved to 7-2 on the season. "Like, as a kid, it's a dream, and you never know if you ever get that first touchdown when you get here. I still know exactly where my first touchdown football is. I know how important it is to me whenever people come to the house and ask about it. So I know when you score, you're just celebrating, not really paying attention to what's going on, so I make sure to grab that, so they have that memory, because they've worked their entire life to be here." The Chiefs easily won in Atlanta on Sunday, and did so without their leading rusher, Kenneth Walker, or without three starting offensive linemen for most of the game. Mahomes had injured his throwing elbow last week, so he was "a little nervous" and unsure about whether he'd be able to drive the ball downfield at full strength. Mahomes had a 50-yard throw to Rashee Rice, the 43-yard touchdown to Armstrong and a 39-yard touchdown to Allen, all adding up to a 348-yard day. It was his first five-touchdown game since 2022 and a 135.5 passer rating, somehow the sixth-best in his 10-year NFL career. "As the game went on, guys stepped up and made plays happen," Mahomes said, noting an early injury to Travis Kelce that limited him to one catch the rest of the game. "We were able to get a lot of guys involved. There were still missed opportunities out there, but it was good to see other guys step up and make plays." Even when they're not at full strength, the Chiefs are balanced and well-rounded, winning on both sides of the ball and with both halves of their offense. Atlanta is in last place in the worst division in the NFL, but the Falcons have beaten the Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers. This was easily the Chiefs' best showing since a season-opening 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos, as the defense kept Falcons star Bijan Robinson in check and held the Falcons to three points midway through the fourth quarter. "We did a good job of playing cohesive defense, staying together," linebacker Nick Bolton, who had a game-high nine tackles and a forced fumble, told me following the win. "It's a long season, and we're just trying to build momentum as the season keeps going. Every team I've been on hasn't looked the same, even getting to the Super Bowl. This is no different, playing week by week." With Sunday's win, the Chiefs exceeded their win total for all of last season, a 6-11 campaign that saw Mahomes injured and not himself when he was healthy. But before that, they'd been to the Super Bowl three years in a row, winning two of them, so this is a locker room still guided by core leaders whose confidence comes not from first-touchdown mementos, but championship rings. It's still too early to call them the team to beat in the AFC. The Jacksonville Jaguars, Denver Broncos and Cincinnati Bengals are also 7-2, and the only team with a better record is the Buffalo Bills (8-1), who host the Chiefs in their new stadium on Thanksgiving night. The winner of that game will be seen as an AFC favorite, both loaded with playoff experience. But this Chiefs team has an added element: impact rookies. Johnson, a fifth-round pick from Nebraska, has shown promise in small glimpses, but a groin injury sidelined Walker late in the week, giving the rookie his first NFL start. He showed he was ready from the opening drive, turning five carries into 36 yards before recording a 12-yard catch on a throw from Mahomes for the first touchdown of the day. He rushed for 101 yards and caught six passes for 70 yards and two scores, a monster game on the same field as arguably the NFL's best back in Robinson. "He did a great job," Mahomes said. "He runs tough, he runs hard, he breaks tackles. Whenever he gets chances in the receiving game, he makes plays there as well. Having Kenneth and how great he's playing, he hasn't gotten as many opportunities, but when his number got called, he stepped in and made plays happen." The youth movement is all over the team, with rookies and second-year players making plays. That includes defensive end Ashton Gillotte, who said he loves this team's combination of upside and experience. "Young blood is good, especially as you get more and more refined," Gillotte, who got his third sack in five games on Sunday, told me. "We've got good vets like KT (Khyris Tonga), George, Chris [Jones]. They keep your head on straight, to know when to rein it back in. It feels good, because we've got a good group." Andy Reid is the oldest coach in the league at 68, but he's surrounded himself with a young team as he tries to get back for another Super Bowl in a truly dynastic run since Mahomes' arrival. "We're one of the youngest teams in the league, and they're getting better every week," Reid said. "It's good the coaches keep coaching them. You have to have a little bit of patience with them, but they're doing a good job." Downs, acquired from the Colts at the trade deadline, could be a missing piece at a position where they've needed help. He and Mahomes had essentially two practices together, and yet the quarterback had the confidence to throw to him in the red zone, well-covered, for an 18-yard back-shoulder touchdown in the end zone. Reid called it a "trust play," excited about the potential of what's ahead. And Downs felt the same way, enjoying his move from a 2-7 team to a 7-2 team. "The fact that I was able to come in here and he's trusting me in those positions, it's nothing short of a blessing," Downs said. "I'm very appreciative. … The coaches are trusting me when I've been here like three days. Pat gave me a chance and I went up and made a play. I'm excited to keep doing that. First game, first touchdown, can't write it any better than that." We obviously don’t know if the Chiefs’ band of newcomers will be ready for postseason success, but Sunday proved that Mahomes can win games with this youthful group. And if they can get more performances like this, then maybe it’s time to start viewing the Chiefs as the Chiefs of old again.

2026 NFL Playoff Picture, Bracket After Week 10
content: The NFL season is past the halfway mark, and Week 10 shook up the playoff race in both conferences. The biggest movement came in the NFC North, where the Detroit Lions took over first place with a 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Munich. The Lions, Chicago Bears and Minnesota Vikings are all 7-2, but Detroit holds the tiebreaker, which leaves the Lions as the NFC’s No. 2 seed behind only the San Francisco 49ers. In the AFC, the Buffalo Bills still hold the top spot at 8-1. The Cincinnati Bengals took over first place in the AFC North with a 38-18 rout of the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night. The Kansas City Chiefs moved into first place in the AFC West, and the loss in Germany knocked the Patriots out of the playoff picture for now. Here is the up-to-date NFL Playoff Picture if the playoffs started right now. AFC Five AFC teams have two or fewer losses, and four of them are 7-2. The Bengals made the loudest statement of the week on Sunday night. Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns, and Ja’Marr Chase had 11 catches for 231 yards as Cincinnati won its fifth straight game. The loss dropped Pittsburgh to 6-3 and into a wild-card spot. The Chiefs moved to 7-2 behind Patrick Mahomes’ five touchdown passes in a 35-13 win in Atlanta. Kansas City and Denver are tied atop the AFC West after splitting their season series. The Chiefs hold the tiebreaker on division record, which drops the Broncos to the No. 5 seed after their bye week. The Jacksonville Jaguars kept pace at 7-2 with a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans, their fifth win this season by at least 17 points. The Cleveland Browns now hold the final wild-card spot. They rallied from a 17-0 deficit to beat the Houston Texans 27-24 and head into their bye at 6-4. The Patriots fell to 5-5 with their loss to Detroit, and the Raiders fell to 4-6 with a loss to the Seahawks. The 4-5 Ravens host the winless Chargers on Monday night. NFC The NFC North remains the best division in football. Detroit holds the tiebreaker for the division lead thanks to its 19-15 win over Minnesota on Nov. 1. The Vikings sit at No. 5 because they beat the Bears 9-3 in Week 2. Chicago was on a bye this week and slides to No. 6. The Bears have lost both of their division games so far, which could come back to bite them if the race comes down to tiebreakers. Minnesota made one of the biggest statements of the day. Kirk Cousins delivered a strong first start after being traded to the Vikings, and Minnesota sacked Jordan Love eight times in a 30-10 win at Lambeau Field. Green Bay fell to 6-4 but still holds the final wild-card spot. The Los Angeles Rams and reigning champion Seattle Seahawks both won Sunday to pull even with the Packers at 6-4, but Green Bay holds the tiebreaker for now. In the NFC East, the New York Giants still lead at 5-3-1 despite a 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night. Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs for the go-ahead touchdown with 57 seconds left. Overall, the NFC has plenty of contenders, aside from the NFC South, where no team has a winning record. The Carolina Panthers beat the New Orleans Saints 20-17 on Ryan Fitzgerald’s 54-yard field goal as time expired in New Orleans, taking sole possession of first place at 4-5. AFC NFC

Brewers Acquire Ryan Walker
content:
The Brewers announced that right-hander Ryan Walker has been acquired in a trade with the Giants.  Right-handed pitching prospects Blake Holub and Gavin Perry head to San Francisco as the return.  Milwaukee has seven open spots on its 40-man roster, so no further moves were needed to accommodate Walker’s arrival.

Walker is projected to earn $1.6MM in 2027, his first year of arbitration eligibility.  The righty was widely considered to be a non-tender candidate in the wake of his unproductive season, and it is possible the Brewers could still cut him loose prior to Friday’s non-tender deadline.  However, Walker’s salary is small enough and has enough of a track record that the Brew Crew probably see him as a bounce-back candidate for next season’s bullpen.

Going to a World Series-winning team with a reputation for fixing struggling pitchers is a very nice outcome for Walker in the wake of a 2026 season that quickly went off the rails.  Heading into the year as perhaps the favorite for saves in the Giants’ closer committee, Walker was rocked for a 6.46 ERA in his first 15 1/3 innings and 16 appearances before he was optioned to Triple-A in May.

San Francisco called him back up a month later but Walker was sent back and forth a couple more times en route to a 7.16 ERA, 14.8% strikeout rate, and 12.3% walk rate across 32 2/3 total big league innings.  The warning signs started to emerge for Walker in 2025 when his strikeout, whiff, and chase rates dropped significantly from the 2024 campaign.

Walker made his MLB debut in 2023, posting a 3.23 ERA, 29.7K%, and 9.1BB% in his first 61 1/3 innings in the Show.  The Giants frequently used Walker as a multi-inning opener in his rookie year, but shifted him into more of a traditional relief role in 2024, with some save opportunities arising at the end of the season.  With a 1.91 ERA, 32.1% strikeout rate, and 5.8% walk rate to show for Walker’s 80 innings that year, it certainly looked like the Giants had found a premium bullpen arm.

Walker essentially has a two-pitch arsenal, as he heavily relies on a sinker/sweeper mix with only the occasional use of a traditional four-seamer.  The righty’s primary two pitches were both fooling batters with aplomb in 2024, but his sweeper’s effectiveness tailed off in 2025, and his sinker followed suit this year.  The sinker’s velocity has ranged from 95.6mph in 2024 to 96mph in 2025 to 95.1mph this season, and a bit of bad luck could be involved since Walker’s .407 wOBA for his 2026 sinker was way above his .328 xwOBA.

Nobody would be surprised if Walker becomes the latest pitcher to get himself on track under the tutelage of Milwaukee’s pitching development squad, making this trade a little risky on the Giants’ part.  San Francisco is prioritizing bullpen additions this winter, and while Walker only added to the club’s relief woes in 2026, it won’t help matters if the Brewers can solve Walker’s control problems and the Giants are left wondering what might have been.

In Holub, the Giants have picked up a pitcher who could contribute to their big league pen as early as next year.  A 15th-round pick for the Tigers in the 2021 draft, Holub was sent to the Brewers in exchange for Mark Canha just over three years ago.  The righty has a 3.89 ERA over 120 1/3 career innings of Triple-A ball, and Holub posted a 2.10 ERA, 28.1K%, 8.9BB%, and a 51.8% grounder rate in 55 2/3 innings for Triple-A Nashville last year.

While Holub spent some of June on the Triple-A injured list, his lack of a big league call-up was probably more due to the fact that the Brewers’ bullpen was already pretty stacked.  San Francisco’s wide-open relief situation gives the 28-year-old Holub a clearer path to his MLB debut, and even a chance to win a bullpen job out of Spring Training.

Perry was an 11th-round pick for the Giants just this past summer, and the right-hander has yet to make his pro debut.  The 23-year-old’s collegiate career was split between former NAIA school San Diego Christian (2022-23), Eastern New Mexico (2024), and then Western Kentucky (2025-26).

Carlos Santana Hoping To Play In 2027
content:
With 17 Major League seasons already on his resume, Carlos Santana is planning to play in 2027, as The Athletic’s Will Sammon, Ken Rosenthal, and Katie Woo reported earlier this week.  Santana turns 41 in April, and he is playing in the Dominican Winter League for the first time since the 2013-14 offseason.

The Diamondbacks signed Santana to a one-year, $2MM contract last February, but he appeared in only eight games before a strained right adductor sent him to the 10-day injured list.  He suffered another adductor strain during his minor league rehab assignment and was subsequently moved to the 60-day IL, and then was activated in the last week of June but subsequently designated for assignment and released.  The Braves quickly signed Santana to a minors contract a few days later, and he hit .293/.389/.380 in 108 PA in Atlanta’s farm system before the first baseman was released again in mid-August.

The eight games marked Santana’s shortest MLB season since his 46-game rookie season in 2010.  Beyond those two years and the pandemic-shortened 60-game 2020 season, Santana was a workhorse for the majority of his career, logging at least 150 games in 10 of his 17 seasons.  As recently as 2024, Santana was still a productive bat, as he hit .238/.328/.420 with 23 homers in 594 plate appearances for the Twins.

This year in Minnesota was a bit of an outlier.  Santana was a quality power bat in his first decade with Cleveland and Philadelphia, but since Opening Day 2020, Santana has hit only .221/.320/.376 over 3133 PA with eight different teams (including a return to the Guardians in 2025).  Based on Santana’s ability to continually find employment, it’s not out of the question that a team in need of first base depth gives Santana a minor league deal and a Spring Training invitation.

The impending lockout is particularly tough on fringe roster candidates in Santana’s situation.  Veterans viewed as pure depth options are less likely to land minor league contracts when teams are still trying to settle larger business before the lockout begins at the end of the day on December 1.  Whenever the lockout and transactions freeze eventually ends, Santana will probably then have to wait out the initial deluge of free agent moves before any teams without enough acceptable first base options come calling.

title: NFL Highlights: Bengals 38, Steelers 18
NFL Shakeout Week 10: Kirk Cousins Is Final Piece To Vikings' Super Bowl Puzzle
content: It was hard to take the Minnesota Vikings seriously, even when they were the last undefeated team in the NFL. It was clear they had a championship-caliber defense. But the way their quarterbacks were playing, they weren’t a serious contender. Now they finally are. That became crystal clear after what the Vikings did to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday behind new (and former) quarterback Kirk Cousins. He showed why they were never going to let the trade deadline pass last week without acquiring a QB, and why he was always their obvious No. 1 target. And he showed why the Las Vegas Raiders probably could have held them up for more than a third-round pick, too. It wasn’t just that Cousins and the Vikings crushed the Packers in Green Bay, 30-10. It was how they did it, and the effect that even a competent quarterback had on the way they played. Cousins put up good numbers in his first start with Minnesota, completing 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. And as usual, defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ unit led the way, sacking red-hot quarterback Jordan Love eight times, forcing four turnovers and holding the Pack to just 220 yards. But Cousins took the pressure off that defense. The Vikings (7-2) held the ball for more than 35 minutes, while their defense was on the field for a manageable 54 plays. And they weren’t forced to merely hold on against a Packers offense that came in rolling. The Vikings jumped out to a 10-0 advantage in the first quarter and led 20-0 in the third. In other words, the defense got to play almost the entire game protecting a significant lead. And Flores' crew can thank the 38-year-old Cousins for that. He kept the offense moving — something his predecessors in Minnesota, Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, could never seem to do. Cousins looked calm in the pocket, not panicked in his progressions. His decisions were good, not forced throws into traffic. His passes were mostly on target, not badly overthrown. The offense looked smooth. He also did it while playing under challenging circumstances. Cousins was the first quarterback to start back-to-back weeks for two different teams since at least 1950. He had to do it on the road, against a strong Packers team that’s been rolling on defense in recent weeks. He had to do it without Jordan Addison, the Vikings’ No. 2 receiver. And he was doing it on a short week, just five days after the trade. But that was the beauty of the deal. The Vikings really don’t need Cousins to do much. He’s not Josh Allen or Joe Burrow, and he doesn’t need to be. He doesn’t have to carry this team. He just has to do what he did Sunday: Be competent, don’t make huge mistakes and settle this disjointed offense down. He’s certainly capable of more. He was playing some of the best football of his career in Las Vegas, completing 64.1% of his passes for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions in nine games on a team with fewer weapons. Now he's back in another familiar system, playing for a coach (Kevin O’Connell) he once thrived under and with an elite receiver (Justin Jefferson) who once thrived with the chemistry they had (nine catches for 74 yards on Sunday). There’s more than short-term potential in Minnesota, too. The Vikings have already leaked their interest in bringing Cousins back for next season, which makes sense. They’re going to have to draft a young quarterback in April. And Cousins just proved in Las Vegas he’s a quality mentor. But this trade wasn’t about that. There was one goal in mind: give the Vikings a chance to ride their remarkable defense all the way to their first Super Bowl appearance in 50 years. Murray and Wentz were never going to get them there — and perhaps not even close to that. They couldn’t even do what Cousins just did to Green Bay. With Cousins, the Vikings are now competent and confident on offense. And their all-world defense now knows it's not alone in the team's title pursuit. The Cowboys want the world to think they’re contenders. They want to make it look like they’re the real threat to the New York Giants in the watered-down NFC East. They want teams to fear their explosive offense. And they swear their expensive defense is always just about to round into form. Yet every week they give more of the same: A weak, pathetic performance by their defense, like what they did in their 46-40 loss at home to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. The Cowboys' explosive offense showed up late, but their defense gave up a ridiculous 584 total yards — the most they’ve ever surrendered at home. On each of the 49ers’ six touchdowns — including (and especially) a 74-yard pass play to running back Christian McCaffrey, a 70-yard run by playmaker Deebo Samuel and a 66-yard pass to McCaffrey with 3:23 remaining that effectually put the game away — they played defense like they had somewhere more important to be. Even after Dak Prescott (343 yards, five touchdowns) pulled the Cowboys within one score with 3:42 remaining, it took the defense just two plays to throw the effort away. There is no amount of Jerry Jones’ "old man" money that can fix this mess. It’s even too late to make a difference by firing overmatched defensive coordinator Christian Parker. The Cowboys had a chance to show some heart and pull off an upset against one of the NFL’s best teams, which would’ve put them on the Giants’ heels in the division. Instead, their defense laid down and blew it. Perhaps the Washington Commanders (3-5-1) are the team the Giants (5-3-1) should really fear. With the Titans and Eagles coming up next, the Cowboys (4-6) have a chance to keep things close in the division. But there’s no real hope, because this team isn’t built well enough nor tough enough to survive even in one of the NFL’s worst divisions. The Cowboys are going to need a huge overhaul and maybe a heart transplant — especially on defense — if they want anything to be different next year. This is a wasted season in Houston thanks to some surprisingly shoddy defense from a club that boasted the best unit in the NFL last year. The Texans are unofficially done at 3-6, after giving away a very winnable game in Cleveland on Sunday. The loss put them four back in the AFC South and 2.5 games behind the Browns for the final wild-card spot — with Cleveland obviously now holding that tiebreaker. Houston will almost certainly miss the playoffs for the first time since DeMeco Ryans took over as head coach in 2023. But there’s good news buried in all the rubble of the bad: C.J. Stroud has reemerged as a franchise quarterback. And the Texans are about to pay him like one, because the 25-year-old Stroud is having his finest season in the NFL. Through nine games, he’s thrown for 2,462 yards with 19 touchdowns and just three interceptions. And he’s doing it after he and the Texans couldn’t come to an agreement on a long-term contract last offseason, undoubtedly giving him something to prove. He proved it, all right, and now he’s in position to set a possible financial record. Franchise QB prices always go up, so he’s a lock to join Patrick Mahomes and Dak Prescott on deals averaging at least $60 million per season. It wouldn’t be a shock if Stroud pushed the bar closer to $70 million per year. With Stroud entering the final year of his rookie deal, the Texans have no choice butt o extend him this offseason. If one thing is clear in the NFL this season, it’s that there aren’t nearly enough quality QBs to go around. Stroud proved he’s one of the few who can play at a high level. He can lead the Texans to a Super Bowl someday, too, assuming they fix their defensive issues. You can’t put a price on a QB like that. Drake Maye may be one of the NFL’s best young quarterbacks. But he’s going to have to prove it all over again next year. On Sunday against the Lions, he hobbled off the field in Munich, Germany, with an ankle injury that could keep him out for a few weeks. It was the latest blow in what's been a disaster of a season for him and the Patriots. But when you factor in Maye's modest rookie campaign, you can't help but wonder if his brilliant sophomore season is the anomaly. It was less than a year ago that he nearly won league MVP and led the Pats to the Super Bowl. But he's since regressed in nearly every area and currently leads the NFL with 11 interceptions. When you look at the pantheon of quarterbacks, he’s no longer up there. He can’t seriously be ranked among the top 10, even though last year it looked like he'd earned a permanent spot in that tier. Among the young QBs, he’s no longer the brightest star. He’s been passed by Caleb Williams (Bears), C.J. Stroud, Brock Purdy (49ers), Trevor Lawrence (Jaguars) and Jordan Love (Packers). Maye is still only 24, but life moves fast in the NFL, and he’ll soon be looking for a massive contract extension — one he may still get sooner rather than later. But he looked like he was on his way to a legendary career when he lost the MVP vote by one of the closest margins in NFL history last season. He’s not on that track anymore. Maybe it wasn’t a fluke. But it sure is going to look like one if he doesn’t bounce back and have a season like that again, soon. Klint Kubiak wasn’t crazy enough to plan to start rookie QB Fernando Mendoza in Week 10 — not against the Seattle Seahawks, and not with the Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns up next before the bye. But the Kirk Cousins trade forced Kubiak's hand and left the No. 1 overall pick in an impossible situation. For a debut start, the 23-year-old Mendoza handled it pretty well. Ignore the middling stats and the 21-13 loss to Seattle and focus on the big picture and what it means for the Raiders' future. Against arguably the best defense in the NFL, one that gives up a laughably low 155.1 passing yards per game, Mendoza played with poise. He completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards while being sacked six times. He also ran six times for 22 yards and a touchdown, adding an element of mobility that Cousins couldn't. Most importantly, perhaps, Mendoza didn’t turn the ball over once. That’s impressive for a QB in his situation. Even more impressive, he led the Raiders down the field for a touchdown on his first drive, which he punctuated with a 10-yard run up the heart of the Seahawks defense. He would complete his first seven passes of the game and lead the Raiders to a field goal on their second drive. Kubiak was smart to limit what he asked the rookie to do, especially knowing that, given the upcoming schedule, things may get worse for him before they get better. That’s OK, though, because there’s really only one way to evaluate a rookie QB at the beginning. Judge whether he looked overwhelmed or incapable of handling the speed and the pressure. And Mendoza, in his first start, looked mostly like he belonged. In NFL Shakeout, Ralph Vacchiano breaks down the impact of the biggest events every Sunday.

title: Former Red Sox, Giants World Series champion retires immediately at 40
content:
Pablo Sandoval played two games with Navegantes del Magallanes of the Venezuelan Professional Baseball League this weekend in Miami. In what proved to be the final game of his professional career, the former San Francisco Giants third baseman connected for a grand slam at loanDepot Park.

¡GRAND SLAM DE PABLO SANDOVAL! ¡EN SU ÚLTIMO JUEGO!

¡4-0 @Magallanes_bbc! pic.twitter.com/cXYUAIfd44

— El Extrabase ⚾️ (@ElExtrabase) November 15, 2026

The three-time World Series champion received a lengthy ovation as he walked off the field in the top of the seventh inning Saturday night, with players from both Magallanes and La Guaira leaving the dugout to applaud the 40-year-old Venezuelan legend.

¡Pablo Sandoval feliz por esta experiencia! 🐼

— BeisbolPlay (@beisbolplaycom) November 15, 2026

For those who weren’t aware Sandoval was still playing, the magnificent end to his playing career was even more surprising.

MORE: Blue Jays’ Anthony Santander apologizes for sharing anti-Muslim videos

Sandoval appeared in the Giants’ spring training camp in March as a special guest instructor. Even though he hadn’t played in an MLB game since 2021, Sandoval continued playing baseball professionally in independent leagues around the world since, and insisted he wasn’t retired.

Sandoval played for the Mid East Falcons of the Baseball United league in Dubai after two seasons with the Staten Island FerryHawks of the Atlantic League. He told the Giants’ website in March that he planned to play for Staten Island again, but that didn’t pan out.

“I continue to play until my body says no,” he told MLB.com’s Maria Guardado.

MORE: Red Sox to sign Brewers postseason hero to $58 million contract

Sandoval retires with a .278/.330/.443 slash line in 1,380 games for the Giants (2008-14, 2018-20), Boston Red Sox (2015-17) and Atlanta Braves (2020-21). He made the National League All-Star team twice (2010-11).

The Giants won the World Series in 2010, 2012 and 2014. Sandoval was named the MVP of the 2012 World Series after he hit three home runs in four games against the Detroit Tigers. In 42 career postseason games, Sandoval slashed .338/.386/535 with six home runs and 20 RBIs.

title: Five Teams Interested In A.J. Minter
content:
The Royals, Rangers, Phillies, Nationals, and Blue Jays are some of the teams involved in A.J. Minter’s market, MLB Network’s Jon Morosi reports.  The veteran left-hander is a free agent for the second time in his career, following the expiration of the two-year, $22MM deal he signed with the Mets during the 2024-25 offseason.

Minter ended up appearing in only 36 games for New York, as a lat surgery in early May 2025 kept him off the mound for a little over a year.  Finally returning this past May 26, Minter posted a 2.56 ERA, 4.3% walk rate, and 22% strikeout rate over 45 2/3 combined innings with the Mets and Twins, as Minnesota acquired the left-hander at the trade deadline.

Given that a hip surgery also cut short Minter’s 2024 season with the Braves, simply getting back to action was a nice outcome for Minter, on top of his solid bottom-line numbers.  The advanced metrics were a little more unusual, as Minter’s walk rate was a career best over a full season (and way below his previous 8.6% career average) while his strikeout rate was a career worst, and significant below the 29.4K% he posted from 2017-25.

Minter’s four-seamer was down to 93.5mph in 2026, after a 94.5mph average in 2024-25.  The velocity drop contributed to the pitch being much less effective than usual, forcing Minter to rely more heavily on his cutter.  A .244 BABIP also helped Minter to that nice ERA, as his 3.52 SIERA was almost a full run higher.  Minter was also more prone to the long ball than usual, as he allowed nine homers in 2026 — by comparison, he gave up only 27 home runs total in his previous nine MLB seasons.

These red flags relegated Minter to honorable mention status on MLBTR’s top 50 free agents ranking, but there’s still plenty of reasons to believe Minter can land another solid contract as he enters his age-33 season.  Minter has been a quality bullpen arm for most of his decade in the majors, he has a solid postseason track record that includes a World Series ring with the 2021 Braves, and he has been consistently effective against both left-handed and right-handed batters.

Now that he is further removed from his hip and lat surgeries, there’s more reason to think Minter could more fully regain his past form, including an uptick in his strikeouts.  It wouldn’t be surprising to see Minter land a multi-year contract, given both the number of clubs involved in his market and the importance of southpaw pitching against the increasing number of left-handed hitters populating big league lineups.

The Athletics’ 5.43 bullpen ERA was the worst in baseball in 2026, but the Royals (5.07) and Nationals (4.99) were the next two teams on the list.  Minter would provide a huge upgrade to either relief corps, but the scale of the bidding could be a factor.  Kansas City doesn’t spend much in general, and while the rebuilding Nats have little in the way of payroll commitments, Washington reportedly isn’t planning to invest much in its bullpen expenditures.

Minter was born in Tyler, Texas and he played his college ball at Texas A&M.  This might give the Rangers a bit of an edge on the field if Minter wants to play close to home, and the team might view Minter as a replacement if left-hander Tyler Alexander signs elsewhere.  The Rangers technically have several left-handed bullpen options already, but Jacob Latz is the closer, Robert Garcia missed most of 2026 due to shoulder inflammation, Cody Bradford could be rotation depth or even a full-on member of the starting five if someone is traded, and Minter is much more established than rookie Robby Ahlstrom.

The Rangers’ bullpen was also a weak link last year, with a 4.47 ERA that ranked 23rd of 30 teams.  The Phillies were 21st with a 4.43 ERA, but Philadelphia’s southpaw relievers combined for a 5.12 ERA — second-worst in the sport, ahead of just the A’s.  The Phillies have already been linked to several free agent relievers but they’re unsurprisingly prioritizing left-handed arms, and Minter is a familiar face from all his time pitching for Philadelphia’s NL East opponents.

Mason Fluharty led all of baseball with 83 appearances in 2026, in part because the Blue Jays rarely had another left-handed relief option to help cover the workload.  Brendon Little got on track in the final two months after a brutal start to the season, but adding a proven veteran like Minter would certainly add a lot more stability to the left-handed side of the Toronto pen.

content:
The Arizona Cardinals turned to rookie quarterback Carson Beck in Week 10, as he made his first NFL start against the Los Angeles Rams. For the big moment in his career, he had a special fan in attendance: sister Kylie Beck.

Kylie, who is a cheerleader for the Miami Dolphins, got to take the week off to support her brother at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, and she showed up in a big way.

After the game, Kylie took to social media to show off her custom game-day fit from Sunday afternoon, flexing the look to her more than 24,000 followers on Instagram. Kylie appropriately rocked a Carson Beck jersey, but added some personal flair at the bottom.

She rocked a custom denim skirt with Beck’s number and the Cardinals logo, along with a “Cardinals” inscription and some extra bedazzling. She certainly understood the assignment for his NFL debut.

Drake Maye injury update could spell doom for Patriots’ playoff hopes
content:
Trouble could be brewing for the New England Patriots after an embarrassing loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich on Sunday morning. Unfortunately, along with the record taking a hit, the team may have suffered an even bigger loss in star quarterback Drake Maye.

Maye exited Sunday’s Week 10 clash in the first quarter after being sacked by Aidan Hutchinson. He was ruled out shortly after limping to the locker room, but there were no immediate updates.

Now, we are learning more.

According to NFL insider Mike Florio on Football Night in America, the Patriots “expect that he will be out a while.”

MORE: NFL fans can’t get enough of massive beers at Patriots-Lions game in Germany

Drake Maye Could Miss Extended Time With Ankle Injury

Mike Florio provides injury updates for Drake Maye, A.J. Brown and Aidan Hutchinson. 📺 Sunday Night Football: Steelers at Bengals on NBC & Peacock https://t.co/Fu8KvtkadI

— Sunday Night Football on NBC (@SNFonNBC) November 16, 2026

Maye will undergo further testing to determine the full extent of the injury, but if what Florio is saying proves to be true, it would be a brutal blow to the Patriots’ playoff hopes.

New England is currently in the mix for an AFC Wild Card spot, but if Maye is forced to miss extended time, then Tommy DeVito would be forced into the starting role. That’s not a situation that the team would want to go into, especially with games against the Bills, Vikings, and Chiefs coming up in three of the next four weeks.

We should get official confirmation on Maye’s status as soon as Monday, but for now, all the Patriots’ faithful can do is hold their collective breath.

Christian McCaffrey’s Career Day Lifts 49ers, Earns LFG Player Of The Game
content: Christian McCaffrey ran, blocked and caught his way to his first LFG Player of the Game, and he made NFL history while doing it. The San Francisco 49ers running back scored three touchdowns in a 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys, including a career-long 74-yard receiving score. McCaffrey finished with 223 yards from scrimmage, catching four passes for 161 yards (two of them were touchdowns) and rushing 13 times for 62 yards and a touchdown. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 50 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in the same game. Brady, who called the game on FOX, opened by asking about the long touchdown, a play that began with McCaffrey staying in to block. He wondered whether McCaffrey was thinking about the record while in protection. "Not at all," McCaffrey said. "I think in that look especially, that might be the first time going into protection, having to wrap for whoever comes in the backside A-gap, and then Brock doing a good job keeping his eyes downfield and playing ball. After that, it was backyard football. Right place, right time, and that was awesome." Brock Purdy rolled right and found McCaffrey, who caught the ball and raced to the end zone to give San Francisco a 17-16 lead in the second quarter. He added a 16-yard rushing touchdown and then a 66-yard receiving touchdown in the fourth quarter. With the 74-yarder and the 66-yarder, McCaffrey became the first running back in NFL history with two receiving touchdowns of 65-plus yards in the same game. Brady also asked about Keenan Allen, who had five catches for 61 yards in his 49ers debut before noting how much adversity San Francisco has overcome at receiver. "Anytime you get a vet like that who just comes right in and fits in perfectly, you know he’s played so much football. So really, just learning terminology and then getting the reps," McCaffrey said. "It’s such a special offense to be a part of. I do feel like we have so many guys who have had so much success in their careers, and everybody’s just bought into the team. They want to win. We want to play well together. We want to celebrate together, and we love the work." Brady then brought up a video McCaffrey shared this week of him playing the harmonica with his son. "You can run, you can block, you can catch, and you can put your little baby to sleep. Is there anything you can’t do?" Brady asked. "There’s a lot I can’t do, man. Let’s see here. Can’t sing," McCaffrey said. "Yeah, there’s plenty. Trust me. I only show the things I can." San Francisco improved to 8-1 and faces the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City next Sunday.

MLBTR Chat Transcript
content:
Mark P

  • The Weekend Chat is upon us! Let’s dive into your questions….

Kevin

  • Guardians sign any free agents?

Mark P

  • Maybe a one-year contract type, but hardly anything earth-shaking

John

  • What would the orioles have to give up for Marte?

Mark P

  • Feels like one of the infielders would almost have to be involved, to fill Arizona’s hole at second base.  Would the O’s move Holliday this early in his career?  That feels like a reasonable risk for both teams, as the D’Backs would be counting on Holliday to fill the shoes of an All-Star.I’m not sure Baltimore is really an ideal fit for Marte, but then again, his market is so unclear that it’s hard to project.  Plus, Marte could veto anything with his no-trade clause.

Matt Arnold

  • With Bauers signing with Boston, do I roll with Vaughn at first base or explore an outside addition?

Mark P

  • Some reporting from this week indicated that this might be Milwaukee’s direction, with Vaughn plus a prospect or two being given a shot.  The Brewers could always re-evaluate things with an in-season trade.

Ebenezer_Batflip

  • Expectations for the new DH in Boston, Bauers?

Mark P

  • If Bauers keeps hitting like he did in 2026, he’s a major bargain and a great signing for Boston.  Perhaps last year was his peak, but even if he’s even in the ballpark of last season’s numbers, that’s a nice one-two punch with Contreras.

Read more

Gregg

  • Would Katel Marte be a good fit for the Phillies? I’m concerned about how he might fit in the clubhouse.

Mark P

  • This has to be the top question for any Marte suitor right now. Can a new team trust that Marte won’t keep skipping games, and if he does, how will a new clubhouse react?It’s an unusual enough situation that frankly, if I’m another team, I’m tempted to just stay away from Marte entirely.

Michael Young

  • With the number of incoming free agents coming over from Japan, Korea, and Taiwan, are the Rangers inclined to make a potential splash in that market?

Mark P

  • Unless the Rangers can unload one of their big four contracts, they might not do anything splashy in the North American market, let alone overseas

Cards Fan

  • Gorman traded or DFA’d?

Mark P

  • Maybe there’s another team out there who thinks they can fix him, but my guess is that Gorman is non-tendered by Friday’s deadline

Campbell

  • DFA candidate? Would he get claimed?

Mark P

  • I assume this is a reference to Kristian Campbell, and no, no team would claim that contract on the waiver wire.  DFA’ing and then outrighting Campbell would be a safe move for Boston, since either Campbell clears waivers and the Sox have extra 40-man space, or another team makes a surprise claim and gets a hefty contract off Boston’s books

Blake

  • What does Nathaniel Lowe’s contract look like? Will he get a multi year dear or just a year?

Mark P

  • He did well enough in 2026 that Lowe probably lands a low-level guaranteed deal, rather than the minors contract he signed last offseason.  But, certainly not more than one year, and another minor league contract wouldn’t shock me.
  • Lowe’s the type of “backup plan” first base option that will probably have to wait out the lockout and then the post-freeze signing frenzy to find his next team.  I kind of wonder if he’s even consider a deal overseas just to avoid the uncertainty.

RJ

  • Do you expect the Mariners to actually deal one of their starters? Or will they just try to clean up the edges as always instead of doing something big?

Mark P

  • My initial take was that the Luis Castillo deal probably marked the end of the Mariners’ rotation trades, but if the team can’t add another bat or two via free agency, they might be forced to move a starter

Astros Leadership

  • Not Astros’ leaderhsip related, but how many AAAA players sign an international contract just to avoid the uncertainty? I can imagine a potential lockout costing a lot of games, would teams in Japan/Korea/etc just release a player if a MLB opportunity were to present itself?

Mark P

  • NPB/KBO teams aren’t going to fill one of a limited number of international roster slots on a player who is signing just as a time-filler until a CBA is settled. Perhaps if the int’l team can line up another signing to take the place of a released player, sure, but you’d think the clubs want guys there who are committed

Jukeboxbrad

  • Am I the only White Sox fan thinking Grant Taylor to the rotation is a mistake?

Mark P

  • The “if it ain’t broke….” argument is very valid, but it also makes sense that the Sox want to see what they have in Taylor as a starter. He’s only 24 and was a second-round pick, so it seems too soon to commit him to bullpen duty forever.
  • If Taylor struggles as a starter, the Sox can always just move him back to the pen

Jim

  • Hunter Greene, and Matt McLain for Ketel Marte? Marte has baggage. Greene will miss most if not all season and McLain still has upside. Risk for both sides. Who says no?

Mark P

  • Arizona.  The D’Backs still want to win something in 2027, and this trade doesn’t really help the team at all for next year.  And even the future upside is a question mark given Greene’s health history and how McLain has done basically nothing since 2023

Nate Lowe

  • You suggested going overseas rather than wait out the uncertainty of a lockout. Instead might I be more likely to take a lowball 1-yr contract right nos from a MLB team?

Mark P

  • If one is available in guaranteed fashion, sure.  But, if you’re a team with a need at first base, do you want to lock in Lowe now or spend more time searching for more productive options?

Joey Ortiz and Garrett Mitchell

  • Your gut…are we both playing in Milwaukee next year?

Mark P

  • Yes

Preller Jr

  • Pads in on Skubal? Sounds like posturing to me. I’d rather they take that $50m/yr and grab two or three SPs off the market. Small to mid market teams can’t survive if he gets hurt. Thoughts?

Mark P

  • The Padres aren’t really a small-to-mid market, however.  A committed and rabid fanbase, plus a San Diego sports market all to themselves, give or take the MLS team and college sports.
  • If ownership is willing to make the splash, signing Skubal is obviously a terrific move, since he’s arguably the best pitcher in baseball.  Having a true ace atop the rotation checks one big box already, and gives the Padres a bit more leeway in addressing the rest of their starter needs

Craig Breslow

  • Arias, Abreu, Gonzalez, Delzine enough for Elly?

Mark P

  • This is the type of offer Cincinnati would heavily think about, and would probably ultimately take. It’s enough of an offer that I kinda doubt the Sox would float it, actually.

Mickey Moniak

  • Could Rockies deal him acquire back of rotation starter?

Mark P

  • Moniak doesn’t have much trade value, as a player who can’t hit righties or hit outside of Coors Field

Pretenders

  • Given that the Cubs are apparently already out on Skubal, can they really be truly considered contenders? Not even trying for a top of the line SP when their rotation is basically empty in a huge market indicates that the team isn’t serious on competing, and there are a lot of regression candidates (will PCA really put up 10+ WAR every year)

Mark P

  • Entirely agree.  There’s no reason the Cubs “couldn’t” be in on Skubal, as the organization prints money.

WNBA

  • Thoughts on WNBA draft lottery???

Mark P

  • The Tempo won!  Go local team!

Guest

  • Are the Jays going to add Brandon Lowe.

Mark P

  • He’d make a lot of sense as a lineup upgrade, and Lowe is more proven at the MLB level than a player like Sato

Tim

  • Angels going to have the richest owner soon, but with the ownership in transition, they’re just going to accept that next year is a lost season?

Mark P

  • Nobody expected a new ownership group/front office to fix things in a year anyway.  Once everything is in place and the lockout is over, you could see the Angels start making some notable moves (i.e. trading people) at the 2027 deadline.

Barry

  • Is the Brewers trade for Walker a flyer on a former closer or is this an indication of where things stand on Megill?

Mark P

  • Basically a flier.  While it’s very likely Megill will be dealt, trading for a pitcher like Walker is something the Brewers would’ve done anyway.

DD

  • No way Lowe plays on that turf after all his injuries. Anyway who is playing right field for the Phillies next year?

Mark P

  • Toronto has an open DH spot to get Lowe some rest days, or the Jays could sit him entirely against some left-handers.Harper isn’t the everyday answer in RF, but he might moonlight there often enough that the Phillies would look for a right-handed hitting outfielder to operate in a semi-platoon capacity.
  • Or, they make a much bigger move and go for Suzuki or Arozarena

Ballyhooed Plausibilities

  • If a player with 10 and 5 rights gets traded (with their consent), do they still have no trade protection with their new club? Or is the “5” reset now

Mark P

  • Once you hit 10-and-5 status, you have it for the rest of your career

Marky Mark

  • Mark, thanks for the Sunday Night Chat!  What is on your Playlist tonight? The world wants to know!

Mark P

  • I opted against my usual random playlist for U2’s new album.As I was buying the physical CD (for my collection) at the record store the other day, the clerk says to me “hey, U2, they’re my dad’s favorite band!”  A real old man moment for me, haha

Phils Fan

  • Is Kerkering enough to get Paraedes from the Astros?

Mark P

  • Not even close

GM of Braves

  • Does Gray 2yrs. $50M and Mahle 2yrs.$24.M sound workable?

Mark P

  • Mahle can likely top that given how well he pitched after the trade.  MLBTR had him projected for 3/$54MM, so unless his market doesn’t develop or he’s willing to give the Braves a bit of a discount, Atlanta would have to bump up that offer.
  • We had Gray at 2/$55MM, so your idea is in the ballpark
  • fwiw, as much as people push Gray to the Braves for geographical reasons, don’t forget that a lot of players live in or relatively near Georgia.  The Braves have one of the more underrated geographical advantages of any team in baseball, and they’ve been shrewd in targeting players who want to play close to home.  So in this sense, Gray isn’t their only option.

Guest

  • Are you surprised by how little action we have seen so far?

Mark P

  • Nope.  It’s an uncertain market out there, with probably a lot of teams and players waiting for the first domino to fall.

Orbit

  • Where does Peña end up and what will the Astros get ?

Mark P

  • Pena probably isn’t going anywhere.  While he might walk in free agency next winter, the Astros will have difficulty filling the shortstop role if Pena isn’t there in 2027.

Jim

  • Mark, with the Cubs needing a frontline starter and a cheap stop-gap corner outfielder, would a trade with the Twins for Joe Ryan and Trevor Larnach make some sense? (each on expiring deals, projected $16M combined arb). Who do you think the Twins would want in return in that sort of deal?

Mark P

  • Don’t forget that the Twins trying to win in 2027, so I doubt they’re moving Ryan unless a really huge offer is presented.Larnach is more readily available, especially since Minnesota already tried to move him at the last trade deadline.  With just a year of control remaining, the team’s asking price wouldn’t be that big.  The Cubs also need bullpen help, so they don’t exactly have a Bryan Abreu around to offer the Twins.

More likely extension

  • Who is more likely to get extended: William Contreras or James Wood? Jim Bowden said that their respective clubs would love to lock them in extensions

Mark P

  • Wood seems likelier to me.  Contreras probably isn’t being dealt this winter, but it’s not usually Milwaukee’s style to extend an established veteran.

Big Dog

  • I’ve seen free agents described as “too pricy” for the Nats. Why should they be priced out on any free agent, especially those without a QO? They are set to have the lowest payroll in the league and were competitive last year. Do the Lerners just desperately need to sell?

Mark P

  • The front office may not feel the team is ready to truly contend in 2027, and thus signing a player or players to pricey contracts might not be prudent if the Nationals are more than just a couple of guys away
  • Now, what I think would be more logical for the Nats is to take on another team’s unwanted contract, with a younger player added on as a sweetener.  I use the term “unwanted” instead of “bad” because there are plenty of pricey players around baseball who are still productive, even if not up to the level of their salary

Nj

  • Baltimore a dark horse for Skubal?

Mark P

  • That would be a real stunner, but I guess stranger things have happened.

Robbie Baseball

  • Do you think the Jays will make a big trade for someone like Seager?

Mark P

  • As a Jays fan, I admit to idly spending a few minutes wondering about some kind of trade package involving Seager to Toronto and at least one of Gimenez or Santander sent to Texas as partial salary offset.  But, there hasn’t been any word about if Seager is even open to a trade, and he has the last word given his no-trade protection.

Ken

  • Shea Langeliers is a Boras client, so he won’t sign long-term with the A’s. What are some potential destinations for Shea Langeliers?

Mark P

  • Ask and ye shall receive!https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2026/10/trade-candidate-shea-langeliers…

rob

  • Do you see a major trade happening before the work stoppage or just the smaller ones?

Mark P

  • I think we’re going to see some major deals happen before December 2.  Teams will want to address at least some roster holes before the lockout, and for clubs that aren’t willing to spend in the top tiers of free agency, the trade market is the better route

Reds

  • What’s the fix in Cincinnati?  There is talk they don’t even have a budget yet?  Is ownership trying to sabotage their chances again and waste what might be Elly’s last full year with them?

Mark P

  • I saw that detail from Gordon Wittenmyer’s recent piece about the front office apparently not having a budget yet.  Though, if you’re Nick Krall, obviously you’ve got a pretty good idea about what your spending capacity will be.  Krall isn’t sitting around with his fingers crossed thinking “come on, $200MM payroll, this is the year….”

Wondering

  • Jordan Wicks for Dylan Crews. Who says no?

Mark P

  • Probably the Nats, since they might want a similar ex-top prospect in need of a change of scenery.  Wicks drew some top-100 attention but he wasn’t viewed as a blue-chipper like Crews

Trevor riches?

  • Trevor Rodgers: two short seasons with an era under 4, 2 seasons pitching more than 130 innings and an extensive injury history. He’s projected to recieve a 100 mill plus free agent deal? I dont get it. Can you explain what I’m missing?

Mark P

  • Teams pay based on projections, even moreso than overall track record. Rogers has shown flashes (sometimes extended flashes) of looking like a frontline starter when healthy, and he is entering his age-29 season.

CD collector

  • I just wanted to let you know I appreciate a fellow cd collector.

Mark P

  • To be specific, I’m a huge U2 fan, and I have all of their albums on CD.  So to continue the set, I picked up the deluxe version of the new album that also contained the two EP releases from earlier in 2026.Before Friday, I can’t remember the last time I actually bought a physical CD

Ebenezer_Batflip

  • Am I crazy for wanting to keep Arias and believing he is the real deal? It feels like he might be the biggest star to come out of the Red Sox farm since Mookie.

Mark P

  • It’s not crazy at all.  I realize that Boston fans may been a little underwhelmed by the returns so far on other “can’t miss” prospects like Anthony, Campbell, Casas, etc., but Arias looks like a player who could start in Boston’s infield immediately.
  • I’ve written this before in chats, but the Sox are only moving Arias if they get an absolute premium player back in return

AJ Preller

  • Is it possible for the Padres to sign King, Peralta, Nick Martinez, and Pivetta all in this off season?

Mark P

  • All four seems like a stretch.  But two of that group certainly seems feasible.
  • Mayyyyybe three

Seeing Red

  • What is Gleyber’s market? Would it be too hopeful to think the Reds would sign him?

Mark P

  • Not out of the question.  It’s an open question as to whether or not Gleyber will finally be able to land the multi-year deal that has eluded him the last couple of years, but I suspect he’ll again have to settle for a one-year commitment.That puts him in Cincinnati’s range, though other teams will also be viewing Torres as a short-term, plan B type of addition.  Maybe if the Reds are more aggressive now and view him as their Plan A for second base, they can jump the market.

Guest

  • Could the Reds trade Steer for B Valenzuela?

Mark P

  • Man, a lot of interesting questions from the Cincinnati fans in this chat.  Reds Nation has plenty to talk about tonight!This would be an interesting deal for both sides.  Steer is the kind of multi-positional guy the Jays like, even if isn’t terribly productive against RHP.  Valenzuela might have starting catcher upside, and is more valuable to the Reds than he would be to the Jays as a backup.

Chili Davis

  • Hi Mark- please give me a couple of SP and a RP you could realistically see the Giants going after?  What tier are they shopping in?

Mark P

  • Imanaga, Griffin, Soroka….it’s possible the Giants could aim higher into maybe the Michael King tier of starters, but those guys might prefer joining a more clear-cut contender.
  • As for the relief market, your guess is basically as good as mine.  As much as the Giants need relievers, this is another case where I see them addressing that need through (lower-cost) quantity, rather than necessarily quality. It would make sense if the Giants splurged on one quality reliever to help add some stability to the back of the pen, and then filled out other spots with relatively less expensive additions

Dustin

  • What are the odds at least one GM or POBO is perusing this chat for ideas on their quiet Sunday evening?

Mark P

  • “Looking for ideas” may be a stretch, but tons of people in baseball read MLBTR.

Brady

  • I imagine a some kind of a Seager/Trea Turner swap is a non starter for Texas but my wishful thinking is hoping I am wrong. Thoughts?

Mark P

  • Turner also has a no-trade clause, so yeah, this one doesn’t work

Someone

  • Tyler O’Neill for some used chewing gum found under a bleacher seat.  Would there be any takers?

Mark P

  • This probably isn’t likely since Arizona is looking for left-handed hitters, but if a Marte trade was worked out, O’Neill could be tossed in as partial salary offset

Dodgers Burner Phone

  • Since the genuine collapse during the postseason, why are the dodgers seriously in what seems like only interested in Skubal and MAYBE Japanese guys like Sato? How come its not like off seasons before where we are involved in every free agent?

Mark P

  • Broadly speaking, the Dodgers are “in on” everyone, in the sense that they can afford anyone and can instantly alter a player’s market with one phone call.  This flexibility allows L.A. to monitor things and then swoop in if they feel a deal can be had on a player they like.

Ben D

  • Any chance the Braves can get anyone to take on Profar and his salary??

Mark P

  • It’d have to be an unwanted contract swap, or as a throw-in as salary offset in a larger deal. In any other circumstance, Atlanta eats a big chunk of that money to accommodate a deal.Or, chances are Profar might just get released.

Bieber

  • Shane Bieber 1 year 8.5 million w 15 million club option who says no (and 1.5 million buyout) so 10 million guaranteed

Mark P

  • A lot of teams would love Bieber at that price tag

Cards

  • Does St Louis have room to make a splashy signing?   What players would make some sense to break the playoff drought?

Mark P

  • How many fanbases are rolling their eyes at four years being considered a “drought”?  :)The Cards are another team who probably don’t feel the need to a big expenditure.  This is only year #2 of their rebuild, remember.  While the team did better than expected in 2026, it still wasn’t enough to make the front office feel one big signing can get St. Louis back to the postseason

Ranger13

  • Does personal service contracts signed during a players active career count against CBT. For example could rangers sign Eovaldi or De grom to a personal services contract to reduce the CBT hit.

Mark P

  • The league wouldn’t allow that kind of obvious attempt to run around the system

One year wonder

  • Could the Cubs fall off and into a rebuild letting the free agents walk out the door?   Will they sign a good player?

Mark P

  • One can certainly take some issue with the Cubs’ approach, but the front office isn’t going to just sit on their hands all winter.  Multiple pitchers will be brought in, at least one outfielder will be brought in, and Chicago (on paper) will probably be a pretty good team again in 2027, though obviously a lot depends on the quality of their acquisitions.

Just admit it Mark

  • You have no faith in the White Sox offseason.  I hope they shock the industry and grab Skubal, Gray and Holmes.

Mark P

  • Given the team’s traditional lack of free agent spending, I don’t think I’m wrong to assume that the Sox won’t break the budget this winter.  But, of those three guys, only Skubal is the one that seems entirely outside of Chicago’s price range.

kurt the hurt

  • Will Emilio Pagan be a good closer for Detroit ?

Mark P

  • I like the signing.  The ballpark should theoretically help Pagan cut down on the home runs.

Earl of Chadwick

  • Bees?

Duke of Varmooth

  • Beads!

Mark P

  • See, I’ve got readers handling both sides for me now.

Me

  • Which leftovers is Tampa Bay ending up with???

Mark P

  • Some mixture of….
    1. a few controllable players yet to break out, in a set of trades that makes the rest of baseball go “oh rats, he was available?”
    2. at least one veteran on a low-cost deal
    3. four or five guys you’ve never heard of

    ….and the Rays then win 90 games again

Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth pay touching tribute to Dan Hicks
content:
Legendary sportscaster Dan Hicks died unexpectedly last week at the age of 64.

Since the moment the news broke, those that worked with Hicks have been issuing remembrances of their colleague and offering condolences to those he left behind.

Mike Tirico added his own tribute to the list on Sunday Night Football, and had nothing but the highest praise for Hicks.

Of his style on the microphone, Tirico said Hicks was “No schtick. All substance,” and constantly making those around him better.

“It’s no coincidence that some of the best sports analysts ever shined next to Hicksy,” Tirico said in a tribute package. “Meticulously prepared. A brilliant storyteller. Dan did it all. And when the moment was big, he was at his best.”

Tirico also took a moment to acknowledge Hicks’s wife Hannah Storm, and the relationship they built from newsroom beginnings.

“But this isn’t just the story of a great sportscaster, it’s a love story too,” Tirico said. “With his equally as talented and wonderful wife Hannah, the greatest sportscasting couple of all time. A story that started on the anchor desk at CNN, continued to NBC, and was shared with so many of us for the last 32 years.”

“When the moment was big, he was at his best.”
Mike Tirico honors Dan Hicks as a talented professional, family man, and true friend. https://t.co/YV0AnyCCs3

— NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 16, 2026

Later on in the broadcast, Tirico and his partner Cris Collinsworth spoke more about their relationship with Hicks.

“This has been a tough weekend for all of us at NBC. Tough for us to work tonight, after the passing of a great friend in Dan Hicks,” Tirico said.

“It’s been such a sad week for so many people at NBC obviously, us included,” Collinsworth, who called NFL games alongside Hicks decades ago, added. “But you can’t help but think how much joy and how much humor that man brought to all of us. He was such a professional, but when you were around him and he was doing his impersonations, he was just so much fun, and he is dearly, dearly missed.”

“That picture you see is Danny. That smile,” Tirico said. “That smile was always on his face. When he worked with people, he made everybody he worked with better. He brought out the best in his coworkers.”

Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth remember Dan Hicks on the NBC SNF broadcast. https://t.co/tHx49I6Kpp

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 16, 2026

While Hicks may no longer be with us, several of his calls on the biggest moments in sports will last beyond any of our lifetimes.
