title: Jimmy Connors shares skin cancer diagnosis
content:
American tennis legend Jimmy Connors, winner of a record-setting 109 ATP titles, recently shared a health update that is common to athletes who play outdoor sports.

Connors, 74, revealed at the beginning of a recent episode of the “Advantage Connors” podcast he hosts with his son, Brett, that he was diagnosed with skin cancer on his ear.

MORE: Where is former ATP World No. 1 Jimmy Connors?

Though Connors did not specify what type of skin cancer it was — basal cell, squamous cell or melanoma — he did share that he is six weeks into his treatment. He promised to show viewers the “finished product” when his bandaged ear is fully recovered. This news came as a surprise because Connors looked healthy at the US Open in September.

Jimbo! Pleasure to have you today, Jimmy Connors 🫡🇺🇸 https://t.co/nsLlo22Rdv

— US Open Tennis (@usopen) September 13, 2026

What Connors said

Connors encouraged people to wear sunscreen. He is undergoing multiple surgeries to rebuild his ear.

He commended his medical team which is taking good care of him but urged people to protect themselves from the sun so they do not have to go through this.

Connors is a living legend who has remained close to the game through coaching, broadcasting and now podcasting since retiring in 1996. He won eight Grand Slams and was the ATP World No. 1 in 1974. Connors was one of the biggest showmen and greatest American men to play the game.

3 ways women’s doubles stole the show at the 2026 WTA Finals
content:
The 2026 WTA Finals is now history. Mirra Andreeva swept the singles event, dominating every opponent she faced in the tournament.

Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend won the WTA Finals doubles title in an exciting match against Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini. The score line may show a straight set win, 6-4, 6-3, but the battle between these teams was incredible point after point. What sometimes seemed like a subdued Indian Wells crowd throughout the tournament got into it with loud and cheerful applause supporting the teams in the final.

Siniakova and Townsend’s win capped off the women’s doubles event which stole the show at this year’s WTA Finals for three noteworthy reasons.

MORE: Taylor Townsend has relatable working-mom moment at 2026 WTA Finals

Good sportsmanship

With the exception of Jelena Ostapenko not congratulating Gabriela Dabrowski, the doubles teams were highly respectful and complimentary of each other. There was a lot less drama and friction in doubles.

Jasmine Paolini’s runner up speech was so full of praise for the tournament, her opponents, and everyone who came out to support them that the crowd gave her huge applause. She also enjoyed a sweet moment with Townsend’s five year old son AJ.

Things we love to see 💚 #FAGEWTAFinals | #TheUltimateStage https://t.co/txTF7ZgyHT

— wta (@WTA) November 16, 2026

MORE: Katerina Siniakova vying for rare WTA doubles achievement in Wuhan Open final

Better photos than singles

For various reasons, the women’s doubles photos were so much better than the singles photos. The teams looked better and handled the awkwardness of going from a group shot to team shots better than the singles players did who had admittedly a bigger transition.

The best doubles teams in the world 💫 The 2026 FAGE WTA Finals doubles portraits 💚 #FAGEWTAFinals https://t.co/ADFw1tINER

— wta (@WTA) November 6, 2026

Kristina Mladenovic, the reigning Wimbledon doubles champion, won tennis fans respect for speaking out about the photo shoot and explaining that she wore her own clothes because she did not like the creative direction and styling of the shoot.

Legends in the draw

Katerina Siniakova, Sara Errani, and Su-wei Hsieh were members of three of the eight teams. Between them, they won 133 WTA doubles titles.

Watching the best of this generation play doubles on the biggest stage was a treat. Their tactics and dexterity were incredible.

Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend,Martina Navratilova https://t.co/EbP4iqnbEj

— Ken McKinnon (@mckinnon88877) November 16, 2026

The bonus was having the greatest doubles player of all time, Martina Navratilova, winner of 177 WTA doubles titles, present trophies to both teams.

title: ‘Big Noon Kickoff’ to go where ‘College GameDay’ has never gone before
content:
Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff is set to make some history this week.

On Sunday, the show announced that it would be heading to Big Rapids, Michigan this Saturday where Ferris State is set to host Truman State in a Division II playoff showdown. It’s the first time that either Big Noon Kickoff or College GameDay have ever broadcast from a Division II school.

FERRIS STATE, ARE YOU READY!?!

Big Noon Kickoff is making history in Big Rapids with its first-ever visit to a Division II school! https://t.co/kA4zCE2Fhv

— Big Noon Kickoff (@BNKonFOX) November 15, 2026

It’s an interesting pivot for Big Noon Kickoff, which is, as its name implies, usually tied to a Big Ten or Big 12 program, and often to whatever big game is kicking off in the noon window on Saturday. While there have been exceptions when Fox had broadcast rights to other big games involving marquee teams, Big Noon Kickoff has not traveled to anything close to the wide variety of programs GameDay has visited over the years.

With its decision to broadcast from Ferris State, the show is planting a flag in territory that its ESPN counterpart has yet to reach. And given the widely positive response that the news has gotten, it looks like a solid move.

Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff show is going to Division II Ferris State this week.

This rules. Huge credit for creativity. Ferris State has won 41 straight games.

— Chris Vannini (@ChrisVannini) November 16, 2026

This is awesome. Well done.

— Jason Scheer (@jasonscheer) November 15, 2026

How cool is this?

— Anthony Broome (@anthonytbroome) November 16, 2026

In a time in college football when everything is slanted toward the major conferences… it’s really cool to see the “little guy” get some love. Ferris State among one of the most dominant programs in the country.

— CFBGrids.com (@CFBGrids) November 16, 2026

As several of the above posts make clear, Ferris State is not just any D-II program. With a 63–20 win over Roosevelt University on Saturday, the Bulldogs hit 41 wins in a row, setting a new D-II record for consecutive victories. Ferris State is ready to party, and to kickstart its run to a potential third straight championship, and Big Noon Kickoff seems happy to bring one to them.

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by NCAA Division II (@ncaadii)

Since its inception in 2019, Big Noon Kickoff has tried out several new ideas in an effort to make an impression on the media sphere that added up to more than sitting in the shadow of its more established counterpart in College GameDay.

At first, the show was only on location for select, big matchups like The Game, and the 2020 COVID season meant that even fewer shows could be taken on the road. But in 2021, Big Noon Kickoff started hitting the road regularly, though nearly always at Big Ten or Big 12 schools. Of the 92 episodes that Big Noon Kickoff has been on location for, Ohio State has been featured in 28 of them, serving as the host 19 times, though some of those were technically conference championship games played at neutral sites, rather than in Columbus. Still, you get the picture.

The broadcast from Ferris State is a big move not only because it gives Big Noon Kickoff a feather in its cap that GameDay does not yet have, but also because it opens the door for more potential alternative destinations for the show next season. While GameDay does a pretty good job of spreading itself out — its trip to Boise this past weekend was a credit to its versatility — one of the greatest strengths of college football is its width.

There is compelling college football that loads of people care about all over the country, and if GameDay is going to spend half of its shows highlighting the SEC, there is a lane open for Fox should the network decide to take it.

title: 49ers Offense Runs Riot Over The Cowboys: 3 Takeaways From San Francisco's Win
content: It was technically a road game for the 49ers, but it certainly didn’t sound like one, with San Francisco fans taking over Jerry World. The Niners gave their traveling fans a show, racking up 584 yards of offense, the most the Cowboys have ever given up at home, en route to a 46-40 win that moved San Francisco’s record to 8-1. Quarterback Brock Purdy caught fire early and never cooled off, and running back Christian McCaffrey put on a vintage performance, racking up 221 yards from scrimmage, including 161 receiving yards. Cowboys QB Dak Prescott tried his best to keep up, but the Cowboys' defense just couldn’t get enough stops down the stretch. It’s been a familiar story for Dallas all season. Now sitting at 4-6, this team has fully exhausted its margin for error. Here are my takeaways: No matter who the 49ers trot out there at receiver, the offense just keeps rolling. Purdy deserves a lot of the credit. His playmaking out of structure was a significant factor in Sunday’s win, as it has been all season. McCaffrey and receiver Deebo Samuel also made their fair share of plays in Dallas. But it’s hard to imagine this group of players having this much success if any other coach were calling the plays. Shanahan has been one of the league’s top play callers for well over a decade, and we might be watching his best coaching job yet. Even with the receiver room decimated by injuries — with the top four receivers out —San Francisco has the league's most efficient passing game. Shanahan also has the run game rolling while not putting too much on McCaffrey’s plate. The Cowboys had no answers for everything Shanahan threw at them on Sunday. The run game consistently churned out positive gains, with a few explosives mixed in, setting up the passing game for success with misdirection plays. Wide receiver Keenan Allen, making his first start for the team after the trade from Indianapolis, fit in seamlessly, catching five passes for 61 yards. George Kittle did what he typically does, moving the chains with tough catches. And Samuel is playing like he’s back in his prime. He broke open the game with a 70-yard touchdown run on a reverse. That was the longest run of his eight-year career. McCaffrey also set a career high on this 74-yard catch-and-run after some brilliant improv from Purdy. McCaffrey iced the game with another big play in the passing game, beating edge Von Miller on an option route out of the backfield and racing to the end zone. The 49ers have scored at least 30 points in five games this season. If you were just looking at the results, you wouldn’t know how injured this unit has been. Shanahan has had to call the offense without all his pieces, but he’s getting the most out of the ones available. No coach is maximizing their talent quite like him. Purdy had been sacked only eight times coming into Sunday’s game. The Cowboys got him five times and pressured him on several other snaps. The defensive front did as well as anyone could have reasonably expected. Unfortunately, the secondary didn’t do its part, so all that pressure amounted to little, and the 49ers still marched up and down the field. That’s been the case far too often this season, and it doesn’t seem to matter what first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker does with the scheme. On Sunday, he turned up the man-coverage dial to simplify things for his secondary, which has struggled to pick up his complex "match" zone coverages. The Cowboys’ 54.3% man coverage rate was easily their highest rate of the season, and … the shift in strategy didn’t yield the desired results, with Purdy going 12-for-16 for 273 yards and three touchdowns. We can’t fault Parker and the Dallas front office for not trying to change things. Parker has tried (and failed) to improve things with different schemes. The team drafted Ohio State safety Caleb Downs in the first round and made a midseason trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The former Steeler has been fine since coming over from Pittsburgh, but Downs has been a disappointment, and cornerback DaRon Bland hasn’t played up to his salary. The team is running out of time to find answers on how to fix this defense, but I’m not sure one exists based on what we saw on Sunday. The 26-year-old lost some early-season momentum and ground to guys like Joe Burrow (Bengals) and Josh Allen (Bills) over the last few weeks, but Purdy’s MVP campaign is back on track after Sunday. Purdy’s playmaking stood out in Dallas. He was under constant pressure on Sunday, and it never seemed to rattle him. He remained patient in the pocket when options opened up downfield. When they didn’t, he went into creation mode, breaking the pocket and keeping his eyes downfield. The big play to McCaffrey was just one of several examples of Purdy creating his own offense. Purdy threw for 135 yards on scramble drill plays. That ties Patrick Mahomes (Chiefs) and Allen for the most in a game since at least 2018, per Next Gen Stats. He attempted just two scramble runs but picked up 21 yards on them. Shanahan also made good use of Purdy’s mobility, getting him outside the pocket on designed rollouts and bootlegs. Purdy hardly missed a throw on the run, completing 4-of-5 passes for 71 yards. The next few weeks could determine Purdy’s MVP fate. He’ll take on Minnesota in primetime next Sunday night before taking on the Seahawks. If he can lead the Niners to wins while putting up numbers against two elite defenses, he’ll have a strong argument for the award, along with a favorable schedule down the stretch. 3 ½. What's Next? The 49ers offense will face its biggest test of the regular season over the next two weeks. Up next is a matchup with the Vikings and defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Pass protection will have to be much better if the offense is going to have a chance to put up points against the NFL’s stingiest defense. Then the Niners return home for a rematch with the Seahawks. If they can win that game, the NFC West will be all but wrapped up. They’ll also have the inside track to the NFC’s top seed. The Cowboys still haven’t strung together two consecutive wins this season, but they’re still in the thick of the NFC East race. They’ve got two winnable home matchups against the Titans and Eagles before the schedule gets tougher. Dallas can’t afford to drop those games, with a tough three-game stretch against the Seahawks, Rams, and Jaguars following.

title: Spain's Unbeaten Streak Snapped: 3 Takeaways From Nations League Action
content: In a scintillating, breathtaking evening inside a pulsating Metropolitano stadium in Madrid, we witnessed a night of high-octane UEFA Nations League drama in the Spanish capital. The prelude before kick-off carried deep emotion, with Spain paying tribute to goalkeeper Jesús de Miguel following his tragic death. And after 43 matches, for the first time since March 2024, Spain — the World Cup champion and almost omnipotent goliath — has fallen. England, with 10 men from the 63rd minute, held on to a remarkable, resilient 3-2 victory and achieved its tenth straight victory away from home. Thomas Tuchel’s side also won the group and will be in the driver’s seat for the quarterfinal stage of the tournament. There were heroes everywhere for England, especially as they desperately held on against Spain, who felt energized after midfielder Elliott Anderson’s red card in the second half, due to being the last man who brought down Lamine Yamal inside the box. We’ll get to them in a moment, but for now, the leading headline takes precedence and that’s this one right here: Spain has been defeated. And it’s all down to a heroic display from the Three Lions. Here are my takeaways: The first half in Madrid was quite honestly the best 45 minutes I have seen from England under Tuchel. We have seen some heroic performances in the past including the victory over Mexico in Mexico City in the round of 16 of last summer’s World Cup. But on Sunday, against the mighty Spanish side, England was outstanding in a pugnacious, aggressive way, and it was because of how it started. And we have to remember once again, this is the World Cup champion. One that hadn’t lost in 43 matches and entered this evening with 12 straight victories. It was almost beginning to feel like numb sentiment to see the side win because it appeared as if nothing could stop it. But at the start of this evening, England did not care one bit about the dragon and essentially echoed the words of Mike Tyson when the former heavyweight champion once said, "Everyone has a plan until you punch them in the face." And that’s exactly what England did at the start. The penalty was a result of a well-crafted counter that started with Anderson. England striker and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane did so well to win the spot kick over Spain's Pau Cubarsí and made it 1-0. Kane has now scored in each of the last seven away matches for the national team, equaling Tom Finney’s record (1946–48). Spain coach Luis de la Fuente made changes immediately in the second half, with defender Dean Huijsen, midfielder Pedri and winger Fermín López replacing Cubarsí, Mikel Merino and Fabián Ruiz. It didn’t matter as the defensive duo of Ezri Konsa and Ben White made it an incredible 3-0. It turned out to be an unbelievable result until a silly mistake breathed life into Spain's chances. England defender Jarell Quansah changed the narrative of the match, when an error forced Anderson to pull Yamal's shirt and be booked for a red. Spain forward Mikel Oyarzabal scored the penalty and Metropolitano became alive as the score was now 3-1 in the 65th minute. Yamal was at it again with a delicious ball to striker Nico Williams, who had just come on, and the Athletic Club star scored again 10 minutes later for La Roja. At this point, Tuchel knew that it was a matter of desperate defending. By now, time was moving ever so slowly for England as Spain continued to press, looking for the equalizer. This is when the ghosts of Argentina crept in as that semifinal loss at the World Cup reminded England fans that nothing is certain in football, especially a lead. But James Trafford refused to bow down. It was a magnificent performance from the Leeds United stopper who had come in to replace Jordan Pickford. Many, including myself, wondered if this evening would be too much for the 24-year-old, especially as the familiarity of Pickford’s starting role was too prevalent for England. But Trafford stood up to the challenge and delivered a magnificent performance, notably with two incredible, quick-double saves that denied Fermín and defender Aymeric Laporte in the space of seconds. The final whistle blew as England left Madrid with a historic victory and this is exactly why the UEFA Nations League was created. To generate rivalries that extend beyond the World Cup or the European Championship. The Spain-England match wasn't the only action on Sunday's docket. France came out victorious over a disappointing but hardworking Türkiye with a 2-1 win. Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi scored his first goal for France, whilst Turkish defender Emirhan Topçu's own goal opened the scoring for Zinedine Zidane’s side. So yes, Les Bleus will be heading to the Nations League quarterfinals after finishing behind Belgium in Group A1. But it hasn't been the smoothest of rides in the first months under Zidane. There were reports of a rift developing between Zidane and star striker Kylian Mbappé, who has been dealing with injuries that have limited him from international duty since the World Cup. The talent isn't drying up for France anytime soon; it's about Zidane managing all those stars. As for Italy? It’s safe from Nations League relegation, but there won’t be a quarterfinal appearance for Roberto Mancini’s side, who had been undefeated in the last four matches before tonight’s loss to Belgium, who earned the 4-1 win thanks to four different scorers including Man City’s Jérémy Doku and Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper. There have been improvements under Mancini, including the rise of young striker Pio Esposito during this window (three goals in two matches).  But sadly, this result was another example that more is needed in order to climb the heights that the Azzurri once knew. It was a humbling evening.

Ian Eagle explains why he knew Ross Tucker would work in CBS’s No. 2 booth
content:
Ross Tucker’s breakout season in the CBS booth hasn’t caught everyone off guard, least of all the guy sitting next to him.

Appearing on Seattle Sports’ Brock and Salk, Ian Eagle told Brock Huard and Mike Salk that CBS asked for his opinion this summer before promoting Tucker into the network’s No. 2 NFL booth. And after calling a long list of Thursday Night Football games with Tucker on Westwood One radio, Eagle didn’t need long to give the network his answer.

“I had done a ton of radio games with him prior,” Eagle said. “So when CBS had to start making some decisions about who’s going to be placed where, and they told me that that’s what they were thinking with Ross and asked my opinion, I said, ‘I know it will work. If the question is, will this work? The answer is yes.'”

The seat beside Eagle opened up during a summer CBS would rather forget, one that left the network scrambling to rework its top two NFL booths just weeks before the season. Tony Romo was arrested in Milwaukee on July 23 on suspicion of drunk driving, and CBS placed him on indefinite leave with no timeline for his return, promoting J.J. Watt to the lead booth alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson. That move pulled Eagle’s partner out from under him after just one season together, and it sent CBS digging into its depth chart for a replacement. The network landed on Tucker, a steady presence on its sixth crew with Tom McCarthy since 2023, and paired him with Eagle and sideline reporter Evan Washburn for at least the first two weeks of the season.

Getting consulted on Tucker was a far cry from how CBS handled Eagle’s last change of partner. When Gary Danielson retired in March 2025, and Charles Davis left Eagle’s booth to become the network’s lead college football analyst, CBS moved Watt off the NFL Today set after two part-time seasons in the studio and slotted him next to Eagle. Eagle admitted he wasn’t consulted, and at that point the only game they’d called together was Netflix’s Christmas Day broadcast alongside Nate Burleson a few months earlier.

Watt exceeded every expectation Eagle had for his rookie year, but the two still had to figure each other out on the fly. Tucker came into this season without that learning curve, since he and Eagle had already called a long run of Thursday Night Football games together on Westwood One radio. At CBS’s preseason media event in August, Tucker said those radio games had given him such comfort with Eagle that he already knew what their TV broadcasts would sound like and how they would feel.

But as valuable as all those years together on the radio have been, the quality Eagle seemed most eager to celebrate with Huard and Salk was the irrepressible enthusiasm Tucker brings to every broadcast.

“It’s not artificial,” said Eagle. “He’s excited. It’s coursing through his veins 24/7 thinking about the NFL. He’s talking about the NFL and that translates on the air. That’s genuine.”

Tucker’s passion came through from his very first Sunday in the No. 2 booth. During Bills-Texans on Sept. 13, Richard Deitsch singled out how quickly Tucker began breaking down a Bills blocking scheme built around left tackle Dion Dawkins, and the reaction that poured in afterward was overwhelmingly glowing. Viewers raved about his excitement on big plays and how comfortable he already sounded next to Eagle, and one fan went so far as to say two minutes of Tucker had taught him more about scheme than years of Romo.

“The guy is so prepared and so into it and eventually people, if they didn’t know him or know his work or know his career, people that watch the NFL, they can tell pretty quickly if someone knows what they’re talking about and actually cares what they’re talking about,” Eagle continued. “So, none of this has been a surprise to me. I’m really thrilled for him that he’s getting the accolades that he’s getting.”

Eagle was just as impressed by the way Tucker has carried himself through the most visible stretch of his broadcasting career, saying the flood of praise and positive feedback hasn’t changed him at all. That was exactly what Eagle hoped for heading into the season. He has broken in a long line of analysts over nearly three decades at CBS, including Dan Fouts, Charles Davis, and Watt, and his advice to Tucker before Week 1 was to trust the approach that earned him the promotion instead of reinventing himself for a bigger audience.

“He’s not changing. And that was a big part of what I mentioned to him prior to the season,” Eagle said. “I was like, ‘Look, all the things that you’ve done have gotten you to this place. So, don’t do something else. Don’t do something different. Go be you, and then we’ll figure out all the other stuff once we get rolling.'”

Eagle brings that same philosophy to chemistry, which he believes has to develop organically between partners. He told Huard and Salk that announcers who try to plan and predetermine how their partnership will sound are usually the ones who run into roadblocks, while the best on-air rapport is often an extension of the conversations two partners are already having away from the broadcast.

“If you have a real honest relationship off the air, that usually can actually translate on the air. And that to me is really what the secret sauce is,” Eagle added. “If we’re having good conversations in the car going to the stadium, why wouldn’t we have good conversations on television? That’s where the line should blur, and it’s been a blast. He really has crushed it.”

10 weeks into a partnership that began as a temporary fix for CBS’s summer upheaval, Eagle and Tucker returned to the booth for Sunday’s Seahawks-Raiders broadcast sounding every bit like the seamless tandem Eagle envisioned when the network first sought his blessing.

title: Orioles Interested In Ketel Marte
content:
The Orioles and Diamondbacks have had some talks about Ketel Marte, MLB.com’s Jake Rill reports.  “No deal was imminent at the time,” Rill writes, and it isn’t known if the discussions were a due-diligence check-in on Baltimore’s part, or if the O’s have a keener interest in the three-time All-Star

Marte’s availability is certainly the biggest storyline of the Diamondbacks’ offseason, yet the second baseman holds all the cards to a potential deal due to his no-trade rights as a 10-and-5 player.  The relationship between Marte and the team may already in an awkward state due to his no-show of a game in Boston in August, which was the most public of a few instances of Marte reportedly skipping out of games in the last few years.  If Marte himself wants out of Arizona, he hasn’t shared any details publicly or even with the D’Backs, as per recent reports.

To further complicate matters, Marte hit .249/.316/.432 with 22 homers over 624 plate appearances in 2026.  This translated to a 103 wRC+, well below the 134 wRC+ Marte averaged in his previous seven seasons.  It remains to be seen if this downturn could be health-related (Marte spent some time on the 10-day IL due to left knee inflammation following the Boston incident), some mental stress stemming from the clubhouse issues, or perhaps just the aging curve as Marte is set to enter his age-33 season.

There’s also the matter of the $91.75MM owed to Marte through the 2031 season.  The D’Backs are reportedly not eager to take on another unfavorable contract as part of a Marte deal, but it’s a substantial enough salary to make a trade even trickier for any team that feels Marte can bounce back with a change of scenery.

The Orioles’ payroll has shot upwards during David Rubenstein’s ownership, and the team’s approximate $127.2MM (as per MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker) on the books for 2027 is well below their $169.3MM payroll from 2026.  While the O’s have several roster needs to address, splurging on a player with Marte’s All-Star ceiling certainly seems like a feasible move, and that’s assuming the Orioles would even have to absorb the entire contract.  It’s possible Baltimore could move some salary back to Arizona by including at least one other big league player in a hypothetical trade package.

It would seem like the O’s would have to make some kind of alteration to their active roster in order to fit Marte, as Rill notes that Baltimore’s infield picture is already full on paper.  The Orioles have Pete Alonso at first base and Gunnar Henderson at shortstop, Coby Mayo and Christian Encarnacion-Strand set for some of the third base duties, and Jordan Westburg, Jackson Holliday, and utilityman Blaze Alexander all in the mix for second base and third base playing time.

How many of these players will all still be Orioles on Opening Day is a matter of debate, as reports have indicated that the team is at least willing to listen to offers for basically anyone besides Alonso.  O’s president of baseball operations Mike Elias downplayed this concept when speaking with reporters at the GM Meetings, saying that “a lot of our key, core players are very unlikely to go anywhere.  We’re talking to everybody about everything right now….But it doesn’t mean we’re motivated to trade players.  It doesn’t mean we’re proactive.  And it definitely doesn’t mean anything is going to happen.  But we’re gathering information here, and I don’t hang up the phone, usually, when people ask about players.”

Some wiggle room could be found within Elias’ statement by wondering which exactly of Baltimore’s infield unit he’d consider true “core players” and which could be more expendable.  But, Elias addressed the playing-time conundrum by saying that some infielders beyond just the versatile Alexander could get some outfield reps during Spring Training.  Rill cited Holliday and Mayo as the likeliest candidates on this front.

Beyond the position-player mix, Elias also noted that the Orioles would “like to retain” left-hander Trevor Rogers.  MLB Trade Rumors ranks Rogers second on our list of the offseason’s top 50 free agents, with a projected contract of five years and $115MM.  It’s no surprise that the O’s want to keep a hurler who has performed so well over the last two seasons, though Baltimore will face plenty of competition from many other pitching-needy clubs.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur doesn’t mince words after Vikings loss
content:
Kirk Cousins and the suddenly offensive-minded Minnesota Vikings beat the Green Bay Packers, 30-10, in Week 10. The Vikings jumped out to an early lead and never looked back as Brian Flores’ defense sacked Jordan Love eight times, and the home fans were booing by halftime.

It was a dominant performance by the Vikings, and the Packers are all alone in last place in the NFC North. After the game, Packers coach Matt LaFleur did not mince his words. He started his postgame press conference with a sobering breakdown of all the team’s problems.

MORE: Emotional Kirk Cousins fights back tears after Vikings’ win over Packers

Matt LaFleur reacts to Packers’ loss to Vikings

Packers HC Matt LaFleur kept it real on the 30-10 loss to the Vikings https://t.co/vhJwlVxywd

— FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 15, 2026

“All right, that was a butt-whoopin’ today,” LaFleur said, per Fox Sport: NFL on X. “This is a humbling league, and tonight, er, today, we got humbled. I think they’re a really good football team and anytime you spot them and turn the ball over four times to their one, that’s a recipe for disaster. Give them credit. They do a great job, but obviously we didn’t coach well enough and certainly didn’t go out there an execute well enough.”

The Packers are headed into their bye week, so they’ll have plenty of time to think about what went wrong against the Vikings. It just might be a bad matchup for them. Carson Wentz threw three touchdown passes in Week 1 as the Vikings beat the Packers, 39-22. Just last week, the Packers beat the Patriots, 45-27, and looked like one of the best teams in the NFL.

Green Bay’s next game is in Los Angeles on Thanksgiving eve. If LaFleur and the Packers spot the Rams any points or turnovers, they’ll be in trouble.

title: Nearby fire fills MetLife Stadium with smoke after Jets loss to Bills
content:
The Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets, 31-12, in Week 10. Starting quarterback Geno Smith suffered a injury and the Jets fell to 2-8 on the season. And yet somehow things got worse after the game when a fire broke out at a very nearby train station.

Well after the game ended there was an announcement over the public address system in MetLife Stadium according to ESPN’s Rich Cimini. The message was a warning that there was a structure fire at the train station outside the stadium and people should stay away from the East side of the stadium. As you can see in the videos below, there was a lot of smoke and it started to pour into the stadium, which caused some people to believe the stadium was actually on fire.

MORE: Aaron Glenn confronts officials, arguing Geno Smith deserves Josh Allen calls

There is a fire by the train station at MetLife Stadium. Smoke is billowing into the stadium. https://t.co/OpWZxXfXMg

— Dan Leberfeld (@jetswhispers) November 15, 2026

So MetLife is on fire. #nfl https://t.co/zf726Tio55

— Michael Mancuso (@M_Mancuso11) November 15, 2026

@Real_RZeroB Metlife is on fire https://t.co/yDAmxpM5L0

— Loki (@lokesook) November 15, 2026

As bad as it looked, Cimini later posted an update on X saying the situation had been resolved. Considering how much smoke there was was billowing out of the train station, that’s an efficient job done by the responding fire department.

The Jets don’t play at home again until Dec. 13 because they have two road games and their bye. However, the Giants are scheduled to host the Jacksonville Jaguars next Sunday. Hopefully they are able to clean up the station in time to allow fans to make a safe and easy commute to the game.

title: Aaron Glenn caught on CBS cameras insisting ‘every flag’ would fly if Josh Allen took the hit Geno Smith did
content:
Aaron Glenn has developed an unfortunate knack for mispeaking at halftime this season, but on Sunday, the Jets head coach finally found words that his long-suffering fan base could rally behind.

Last month, Glenn assured sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala that the Jets would receive the ball to open the second half against the Patriots, only for New England to take the ensuing kickoff. When a reporter asked him about it the following day, the team’s livestream of his press conference conveniently went dark, though Glenn reportedly insisted his words had been misconstrued.

Glenn left far less to interpretation on Sunday, when CBS cameras caught the 54-year-old excoriating referee Ron Torbert and his crew as the teams filed off the field at halftime of an eventual 31-12 loss to the Bills, still incensed over a hit on Geno Smith that had inexplicably escaped a flag in the closing minutes of the half.

CBS cameras capture Aaron Glenn giving officials the business, as he can be seen saying that every flag in the building would’ve been thrown had Josh Allen been at the receiving end of a late hit on Jets QB Geno Smith: https://t.co/f4n73p4JTR

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 15, 2026

With the Jets driving inside Buffalo territory on third down late in the first half, Geno Smith slipped out of the pocket, set his feet, and was folded in half the instant he let go of the football, as linebacker Terrel Bernard barreled into his chest while rookie T.J. Parker dove at his knees. Smith crumpled to the turf and eventually into the league’s concussion protocol, and the officials, evidently satisfied with what they had seen, kept their flags in their pockets.

Geno Smith is down on the field https://t.co/VITOuHm6J0

— Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 15, 2026

Glenn did not share their contentment, and instead of litigating the nuances of the rulebook, he challenged the officials to imagine how they would have responded had Buffalo’s quarterback been on the receiving end of the same hit.

“Here’s my problem with that: if that was Josh Allen, every flag on the field would be thrown,” Glenn can be seen telling the officials.

Given that the NFL has spent the better part of two decades wrapping its quarterbacks in an ever-thickening layer of bubble wrap, to the point where a pass rusher can now be penalized for landing on a passer with too much of his own body weight, you can understand Glenn’s frustration. And it takes a certain creativity to watch two defenders converge on a quarterback from opposite ends and conclude that nothing illegal occurred. Smith had left the pocket, which under NFL rules strips a passer of some of his special protections, including the one against low hits. But the rulebook restores all of them once a quarterback stops behind the line of scrimmage and resets to throw, and Smith had done just that by the time Bernard and Parker arrived to meet him from both directions.

Unfortunately, the letter of the law apparently also requires Gene Steratore to sign off on every call the officials make. The CBS rules analyst assured viewers that the crew had gotten it right, extending a habit of siding with officials that has drawn grumbles from viewers before. Bills fans know that tendency as well as anyone, having watched Steratore give his blessing to the overtime interception that ended their season in Denver last January. On Sunday, Buffalo finally landed on the right side of his rubber stamp.

The Jets, as usual, did not.

title: P.J. Fleck Fires OC Greg Harbaugh Jr. Following Minnesota's Loss To Penn State
content: Minnesota offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. was fired Sunday with two regular-season games remaining following another rough performance by the Gophers. Coach P.J. Fleck announced his decision the day after the 42-14 loss at Penn State, when the Gophers converted three of 13 third downs and were scoreless for more than 38 minutes of game time until finally reaching the end zone. That was Minnesota's sixth straight game with less than 300 total yards. "Greg has been an important part of our football program, and I want to thank him for the time, energy and commitment he gave to our players and university," Fleck said. "These decisions are never easy, but I believe this is the right one for our football team. I have tremendous respect for Greg as a coach, husband and father and thank him for his many contributions to our program. I wish him and his family the best moving forward." Harbaugh was in his third stint on Minnesota's staff, in his fourth season as the play-caller. He was a quality control assistant in 2017 and again in 2019. After returning in 2022 as tight ends coach, Harbaugh was elevated to quarterbacks coach and co-offensive coordinator in 2023. He became the sole offensive coordinator in 2025. The Gophers (5-5, 3-4), who rank 129th out of 136 teams in the FBS in total yards, are averaging 17.6 points over seven Big Ten games. They host Northwestern on Saturday. Reporting by the Associated Press.

title: Pablo Sandoval Announces Retirement
content:
Pablo Sandoval has announced the end of his playing career, after 14 Major League seasons and parts of 21 total seasons in pro ball.  The longtime third baseman is saying his farewell after a few more games with Navegantes del Magallanes, the Venezuelan winter league club Sandoval suited up for at the very start of his career (and at a couple of other points during his two-plus decades as a player).  The Turcos faced Tiburones de La Guaira in a two-game series at loanDepot Park in Miami this weekend, and Sandoval marked the occasion by hitting a grand slam in his final game in a big league ballpark.

“The Kung Fu Panda” last played in a MLB game in 2021 as a member of the Braves.  He played with two Mexican League teams in 2022 and a team in Dubai in 2023, then signed a minor league deal with the Giants during Spring Training 2024 but was released prior to Opening Day.  Sandoval played for the Staten Island FerryHawks of the independent Atlantic League in both 2024 and 2025, and is now officially hanging up his cleats at age 40.

Eleven of Sandoval’s 14 Major League seasons came in San Francisco, where he was an integral part of the Giants teams who captured World Series championships in 2010, 2012, and 2014.  He posted huge numbers during the last two of those title runs, and won World Series MVP honors in 2012 on the strength of one of the most memorable games in baseball history.  Sandoval went yard in his first three plate appearances in Game 1, putting Sandoval alongside Albert Pujols, Reggie Jackson, and Babe Ruth (who did it twice) as the only players to ever hit three home runs in a World Series game.

Sandoval was a career .338/.386/.535 hitter over 171 career postseason PA, and he hit .278/.330/.443 with 153 homers over 5052 regular-season plate appearances from 2008-21.  As per wRC+, his best two offensive seasons were actually two of the Giants’ non-championship years — Sandoval had a 146 wRC+ from a .330/.387/.556 slash line in his first full MLB campaign in 2009, and he hit .315/.357/.552 with 23 homers in 2011 for a 149 wRC+.

A career 110 wRC+ reflects the somewhat up-and-down nature of Sandoval’s play.  While the Panda nickname helped Sandoval stand out as a fan favorite (and made for plenty of memorable pieces of Giants merchandise), he also battled weight problems at various points in his career.  These issues cut into his playing time during the 2010 season, and began to again impact Sandoval’s play after he left the Giants for a five-year, $95MM free agent with the Red Sox prior to the 2015 campaign.

The signing was simply a bust for the Sox, as Sandoval posted a modest .646 OPS over 620 PA and 161 games in a Boston uniform before he was released in July 2017.  He didn’t hit well in 2015, a shoulder surgery cost Sandoval all but three games of the 2016 season, and more injuries (a knee sprain and an inner ear infection) followed in 2017.

Following his release from the Red Sox, Sandoval returned to the Giants on a minor league contract and got into 47 big league games in the rest of the 2017 season.  The next two years saw Sandoval play mostly in a part-time role against primarily right-handed pitching, and he regained some of his old form by hitting .259/.311/.466 with 23 homers in 548 PA in 2018-19.

Returning to the Giants on another minors contract in 2020, Sandoval was released that September and then signed by the Braves for one regular-season game and four PA over three playoff games.  Another minor league contract followed with Atlanta that offseason, and he hit .178/.302/.342 in what proved to be the final 86 PA of the Panda’s MLB career.  Sandoval was released after being dealt to Cleveland for Eddie Rosario at the 2021 trade deadline in what proved to be a critical deal for the Braves.  Rosario caught fire after the trade and won NLCS MVP honors en route to helping the Braves win the World Series, leading Sandoval to earn the fourth championship ring of his career.

Sandoval was one of five Giants players added to the team’s Wall of Fame last summer, and he’ll forever be a legend among San Francisco fans.  We at MLB Trade Rumors congratulate Sandoval on a tremendous career, and we wish him the best in retirement.

title: ESPN announcers remind Duke-Miami viewers that the SEC ‘is the NFL’
content:
ESPN never runs short of places to remind viewers that the SEC plays the best football in the country, and on Saturday it found another one in the middle of a Miami-Duke broadcast.

Matt Glenesk flagged the exchange, which came as ABC’s Miami-Duke broadcast checked in on Alabama’s trip to Vanderbilt. The seventh-ranked Crimson Tide had gone scoreless for nearly 30 minutes against a Commodores team that entered the day 1-5 in conference play, finally grabbing a 7-3 halftime lead when Keelon Russell found tight end Marshall Pritchett for a nine-yard touchdown in the closing seconds of the second quarter.

ESPN broadcasters during Miami-Duke game talking about how close Alabama-Vandy game is:

“That league, it is the NFL. It’s amazing how often the games are in doubt when you don’t think they should be.”

Yes, let’s gloss the SEC some more. But when Big Ten games are close, well…

— Matt Glenesk (@MattGlenesk) November 14, 2026

Cutting away for a score update is standard fare on any college football Saturday. Bob Wischusen, however, treated this one as a springboard for an impromptu sermon on the SEC’s competitive depth, delivered to an audience that had tuned in for an ACC game, and viewers outside the conference were in no mood to hear it.

This is the whole game. When Indiana is struggling with Minnesota it’s an indictment of them and the Big Ten but change out the helmets for network-approved brands and suddenly it’s actually good to struggle against bad teams.

— babar (@babaresq) November 15, 2026

I was watching Bama/Vandy today when this statement was made. If you didn’t cringe I don’t trust your judgement

Vanderbilt is a sub-mediocre FB team on any scale, w/wins over Austin Peay, Delaware, NC State, & the Fighting BFWs

— Mark Schipper – 5th Down CFB (@5thDownCFB) November 15, 2026

Vanderbilt is literally dead last in the SEC. Even Arkansas beat them. It’s reaching ridiculous, collusion levels, and @Big12Conference should sue ESPN.

— The U Fan Cast (@TheUFanCast) November 15, 2026

“It is intriguing, but that league — we’ve talked about it before, Louis — it is the NFL,” Wischusen said. “It’s amazing how often the games are in doubt when you don’t think they should be in the SEC.”

“So much parity,” added Riddick. “It’s great for college football.”

“It is intriguing, but that league — we’ve talked about it before, Louis — it is the NFL. It’s amazing how often the games are in doubt when you don’t think they should be in the SEC.” – Bob Wischusen.

“So much parity. It’s great for college football.” – Louis Riddick.

[image or embed]

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing.bsky.social) November 15, 2026 at 3:24 PM

In fairness to the broadcast, it’s hardly a crime to let viewers know about a compelling game elsewhere, and the booth rounded out the thought by noting that nail-biters benefit the sport regardless of where they happen. But Wischusen went further than that, telling an ACC audience that the SEC is the NFL on the strength of Alabama leading a one-win Vanderbilt team by four points at halftime.

The Crimson Tide scored on its first two possessions of the third quarter, both on Russell touchdown passes to Lotzeir Brooks, and cruised to a 21-6 win while Vanderbilt’s offense managed only a pair of long Brock Taylor field goals and two late turnovers on downs. The loss dropped the Commodores to 1-6 in the SEC, a record that already included a 35-point drubbing at the hands of Ole Miss and a 24-point loss to Georgia.

Suffice it to say, a heavy favorite sleepwalking through a half against one of the conference’s weakest teams makes for flimsy evidence that every SEC Saturday is a coin flip, particularly when that favorite woke up after halftime and won by 15.

The comment would have drawn eye rolls on any network, but coming from an ESPN broadcaster, it played directly into a suspicion that much of the network’s audience already harbors about where its loyalties lie.

Nearly two-thirds of respondents in our 2025 media bias survey said they perceive an SEC slant at ESPN, and eight of the 12 network personalities included in the poll registered a lean toward the conference. Paul Finebaum predictably topped the list with a +97 SEC bias score, but the perception extended well beyond the network’s most obvious conference loyalists, ensnaring College GameDay fixture Nick Saban (+71), game analysts Greg McElroy (+54) and Booger McFarland (+50), and even Kirk Herbstreit (+44), who has spent considerable energy insisting there is no bias to speak of. Fox faced similar accusations of favoring the Big Ten, its own lucrative partner, but respondents viewed ESPN’s lean as both more widespread and more pronounced, with 67 percent of its polled talent flagged for SEC bias compared to 40 percent of Fox’s for the Big Ten.

If the SEC is the NFL, the Big Ten has spent the last three seasons winning its Super Bowl, capturing three consecutive national championships while the SEC failed to even reach the title game. And while the SEC still sends more players to the NFL than any other conference, including a record 87 draft picks this past April, none of that talent has carried an SEC team back to the national championship game since Georgia won its second straight title in the 2022 season.

Sure, it just means more, as the conference likes to remind everyone, but viewers of every other league shouldn’t have to hear about it in the middle of their own games.

KBO’s Hanwha Eagles Sign Troy Watson
content:
The Hanwha Eagles of the Korea Baseball Organization have signed right-hander Troy Watson to a one-year deal for the 2027 season, according to Dan Kurtz of MyKBO. Watson earns a $300K signing bonus and a $700K salary with his new club.

Watson, 29, was a late-round pick by the Blue Jays back in 2018. He worked his way through their system for the next few years, reaching Triple-A in 2023 and sticking at that level the following year. In August 2024, Toronto sent Watson to the Tigers for cash, and he would spend most of the next two calendar years in their system. Detroit designated him for assignment this past August, at which point he got claimed off waivers by the Mariners. Watson elected minor league free agency in lieu of accepting an outright assignment earlier this month.

Watson struggled badly in his first extended run at Triple-A back in 2024. He fared much better in the next two years, posting a 3.12 earned run average in ten starts for the Toledo Mud Hens in 2025, then a 3.47 ERA in 70 innings for the Mud Hens and Seattle’s Tacoma affiliate this year. Watson sits in the low-to-mid 90s with his four-seamer and mixes in a slider, cutter, sinker, and the occasional changeup. In the last three years, he’s had decent walk rates but inconsistent strikeout and ground ball metrics.

The Tigers added Watson to their 40-man roster back in July to keep him from going overseas. He was immediately optioned and only lasted a few weeks before the aforementioned DFA, so he’s yet to make his major league debut. For now, Watson will head overseas and pocket a larger chunk of money than if he’d stuck around in affiliated ball. Depending on how he does in the KBO, perhaps he could return stateside a few years from now in a better position to land an MLB opportunity.

Latest On Brewers’ First Base Mix
content:
The Brewers just saw this year’s first baseman Jake Bauers depart for the Red Sox on a four-year, $58MM deal, contrary to MLBTR readers’ prediction that he would accept Milwaukee’s qualifying offer. With Bauers gone, the Brewers won’t necessarily add another first baseman for the 2027 season, according to The Athletic’s Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal. Sammon and Rosenthal write that the team could retain Andrew Vaughn in arbitration or turn to one of their prospects, while throwing cold water on the team’s chances of pursuing Ty France.

Vaughn is projected for an $8.5MM salary, according to MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz. He appeared in 104 games for the Brewers this year and took 331 trips to the plate. In that sample, he batted .306/.390/.444 with a 134 wRC+. Vaughn was quite productive against southpaws, putting up a 161 wRC+ in 133 plate appearances, though he more than held his own with a 117 wRC+ against same-handed pitchers.

The overall production was more or less a continuation of Vaughn’s output last year with Milwaukee. He came over from the White Sox that June in a cash trade for Aaron Civale, and Vaughn proceeded to put up a .308/.375/.493 triple slash in 254 plate appearances for the Brewers, good for a 142 wRC+. The main differences this year were a decline in power and improved batted ball fortune. Vaughn saw his isolated power decline from .158 to .139, and he only hit six home runs all season. He also batted .355 on balls in play, which is sure to come down.

On the flip side, Vaughn’s Statcast profile shows plenty of red, which bodes well for his continuing to hit in 2027. He has good plate discipline, ranking better than average by strikeout rate (16.0%), walk rate (10.6%), and chase rate (23.5%). The contact quality metrics are also solid. Vaughn hit for a 90.1 mph average exit velocity, 43.5% hard-hit rate, and squared up on 33.9% of the balls he put in play. All three of those check in higher than average, particularly the squared-up rate.

Vaughn could stand to lift the ball more, but given how he’s hit since arriving in Milwaukee, he’s not a bad first option at the cold corner. The team was comfortable with the idea of paying Bauers $23.15MM for one year, so doling out $8.5MM for Vaughn would even be something of a cost saver. The Brewers are currently projected for a $114.4MM cash payroll in 2027, as noted in MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker.

Vaughn’s $8.5MM projection is already baked into that figure. Before factoring in any additional payroll space created by their World Series victory, that leaves $29.5MM of wiggle room before Milwaukee matches its 2026 year-end total of $143.9MM. Vaughn and closer Trevor Megill, who’s projected to earn $8MM in arbitration, have been floated as speculative trade candidates for the payroll-savvy Brewers. Now, Megill seems like the more likely trade candidate. He’s coming off a career-best, 30-save season and could fetch a decent haul of prospects, and the Brewers have several other relievers who could step up as the closer.

The Brewers’ apparently slim chances of pursuing France make sense. He’s now the only starting caliber first baseman on the market, is coming off a great season, and already has multiple suitors including the Mets and the Padres. We at MLBTR expect France will earn around two years and $32MM in guaranteed money, though perhaps he could beat that given the robust interest and the kind of money that Bauers just got from Boston.

Sammon and Rosenthal note that three prospects in the Brewers’ Top 30 are first basemen. Those players are Andrew Fischer, Blake Burke, and Luke Adams; they rank No. 5, No. 12, and No. 13 on the Brewers’ Top 30 list, respectively, according to MLB Pipeline. Fischer put up a 154 wRC+ at Double-A this year and bats left-handed, so he’s theoretically an ideal platoon partner for Vaughn if he makes it to the Majors. Burke struggled mightily upon reaching Triple-A, while the right-handed hitting Adams did quite well, putting up a 149 wRC+ in 279 plate appearances.

There’s risk in trusting prospects, of course, but the presence of Vaughn might help those three ease into the Majors while giving the Brewers more affordable coverage at first base than Bauers or France would have cost. Should the team look elsewhere, Nathaniel Lowe and Josh Bell are among the left-handed hitting (or switch-hitting in Bell’s case) free agent options who could platoon with Vaughn. For now, though, it seems they’ll handle the position internally.

Ian Rapoport mocked for overstating Arch Manning’s game-winning throw
content:
Nick Wright has led the charge on holding NFL insiders accountable for prioritizing self-serving pandering over serving fans by reporting the facts.

Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network is often an easy target, and he painted a fresh target on his back Saturday night.

Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning struggled immensely against the LSU Tigers, throwing three interceptions. The Longhorns trailed by as many as 11 points in the third quarter.

In the fourth quarter, LSU punted the ball back to Texas with a 21-16 lead. Manning led a clutch two-minute, game-winning drive. Manning threw a swing pass to Raleek Brown with three seconds left to seal the 22-21 win.

“Arch Manning with an unreal throw with the game on the line,” Rapoport tweeted alongside a clip of the play.

Arch Manning with an unreal throw with the game on the line. https://t.co/5IWK8Ye55Q

— Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 15, 2026

It is true that Manning showed resilience by overcoming a woeful night and executing when it mattered most. However, most people watching the game recognized that the credit belonged to Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian for his incredible play design, which motioned Brown to scheme him wide open in the flat. If Manning missed that throw, then “unreal” would have been appropriate.

Now that we’ve established the facts, you’ll understand why Rapoport was widely mocked for overstating Manning’s throw.

“Probably the most unreal throw any of us have ever seen. Rapsheet undersold it. Just wow,” Kyle Quinn of 94 WIP posted.

“Is this satire or is Rapoport genuinely calling this an ‘unreal throw’?” Darin Zoccali posted. 

“Unreal throw? That was a 2-yard screen…” Jarah Mcfarlane wrote.

And within the 3,800 replies to Rapoport’s post, there was plenty more where those wise cracks came from. Check out some of the best below.

1) Manning does get overhyped significantly due to his last name and even on this throw.

title: White Sox Interested In Hiromi Itoh
content:
The White Sox are known to be seeking rotation upgrades this winter, and they’ve identified Japanese right-hander Hiromi Itoh as one of their targets. According to Francys Romero of BeisbolFR.com, the Sox sent scouts to watch Itoh and his countryman Kaima Taira in August and September, and they’re expected to be among Itoh’s suitors in free agency. Chicago’s interest in Taira was previously reported.

Itoh, Taira, and infielder Teruaki Sato were officially posted by their respective NPB teams on November 1. Ordinarily, they would have had 45 days to negotiate a contract with MLB clubs, but the looming lockout is throwing a wrench in those plans. The day after their postings, it was reported that their negotiating window would not pause in the event of a lockout, so their 45-day window is effectively reduced to just 30 days. Itoh, Taira, and Sato now have a little more than two weeks to sign with MLB clubs. If they do not, they’ll return to NPB for 2027.

Among the two starters in that trio, Itoh isn’t as flashy as Taira but should still procure a big league deal. He has a 2.91 earned run average and 902 career strikeouts in just over 1,000 innings for the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters. In 2025, he won the Sawamura Award, the NPB equivalent of the Cy Young award. Itoh has also shown excellent control, posting walk rates of 5.5% or lower in each of the last three seasons for the Fighters.

In terms of stuff, the 5’9″, 180-pound Itoh sits in the low-90s but has good vertical break and high spin on his four-seamer. He’s been noted for using as many as ten unique pitches, including a splitter, sinker, sweeper, curveball, and changeup. Itoh’s undersized physique and finesse-over-power approach might make him more of a back-end starter in the Majors. We at MLBTR rank him at No. 36 on our Top 50 Free Agents list and expect him to earn a two-year, $20MM guarantee. Posting fees for NPB players amount to 20% of the first $25MM, so if Itoh matches that projection, $4MM would be paid to the Fighters, bringing the total outlay to $24MM.

General manager Chris Getz has indicated that hard-throwing reliever Grant Taylor will work as a starter going forward. Taylor stands alongside breakout righty Sean Burke, Davis Martin, Anthony Kay, and veteran Luis Castillo in the projected 2027 rotation. It’s a pretty inexperienced group outside of Castillo, and it’s also lacking in star power on the front end. Itoh wouldn’t move the needle there, but he could be an improvement over Noah Schultz, David Sandlin, and Drew Thorpe as far as back-end/depth types go.

The White Sox are currently projected for $108.5MM in cash payroll for 2027, as noted in MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker. That’s slightly higher than last year’s figure, but there should be room for further spending in the wake of the team’s surprise playoff appearance. Granted, the Sox have never given out a contract worth more than $75MM (Andrew Benintendi in the 2022-23 offseason). On the other hand, they have just one guaranteed contract on the books for 2028 (Castillo) and zero for 2029 onward.

So far, the Sox are involved in the markets for Itoh, Taira, and right-hander Dustin May. They also figure to be scouting the trade market, which could feature Reid Detmers, Drew Rasmussen, and others. The payroll space is there to add a back-end guy like Itoh for a modest salary and, theoretically, even an ace like Tarik Skubal, though the team reportedly isn’t involved in his market.

title: Dana White claims he wants ‘nothing to do with politics’ while appearing on Fox News
content:
Kirk Herbstreit pleaded political ignorance in the controversial aftermath of Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) appearing on ESPN’s College GameDay, and a quick search proved Herbstreit’s comments disingenuous.

UFC CEO Dana White just put himself in a similar situation.

White and President Donald Trump have been friends for decades, as ESPN thoroughly chronicled recently, and their ties became front-page news last week.

On Nov. 7, Trump posted on Truth Social that he was “pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States.”

Katie Zacharia served as the White House press secretary for all of five days before she was “forced out of her role,” as reported by The New York Times on Oct. 16.

Conflicting reports ensued, and after swift, universal backlash, Trump claimed he was “only kidding.”

Two days later, White accompanied Trump at his White House press briefing. Trump didn’t sound like someone who was joking about wanting White as the new White House press secretary. During the briefing, he waxed poetic about a world where White was his press secretary.

Eventually, Trump awkwardly asked White directly whether he’d like the job, to which White said, “Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics.”

Over the weekend, White appeared on My View with Lara Trump on Fox News. Toward the end of the 10-minute interview, Trump asked White about his future.

“You’ll never see me involved in politics,” White said. “I want nothing to do with politics. But as far as this business goes, I’m in boxing now. It’s my first year involved in boxing, so I’m just always focused on what’s next with my business and where we want to take it. Places we’ve never been before. My ceiling is eight billion. There’s eight billion people in the world. And when you get the right fight, in the right place, with the right guys, I truly believe that everybody wants to watch it.”

Among the eight billion people alive, some took the time to fact-check White on his claim that he stays away from politics.

“Dana White has spoken at the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Republican National Conventions,” a Community Note reads under a clip posted by The Politics & Poll Tracker account.

Fox News: Dana White says he’s not political and doesn’t want to be involved with politics

“You’ll never see me involved in politics. I want nothing to do with politics.” https://t.co/nreWDAdFH2

— Politics & Poll Tracker (@PollTracker2024) November 15, 2026

“You might have thought based on Dana White’s appearance as a speaker at the 2016 Republican National Convention and then again at the 2020 Republican National Convention followed up by speaking at the 2024 Republican National Convention that he’s actually pretty political,” political pundit Matthew Yglesias wrote.

Maybe one day, people will remember the internet exists before engaging in blatant hypocrisy.

Wake Forest Really Kicked Some Ass
content:
While prognosticators have been wondering who could be the next school to make an Indiana-type leap into the big leagues, with some already crowning UCLA as the likeliest successor, the Wake Forest Demon Deacons have been quietly developing into something of a budding juggernaut. Those are big words for an ACC program that put up back-to-back 4-8 seasons in 2023 and '24, but I don't think they're totally inaccurate.

In Jake Dickert's first year at the helm of Wake Forest, they went 9-4 with a Mayo Bowl win over Mississippi State. In his second year, they are currently 9-1, with their only loss coming against championship favorite Miami. While they have not exactly gone against a gauntlet, they have dominated in most of their games, particularly in the last six weeks, outscoring their opponents 313-38.

This casualty list added SMU on Saturday when the Demon Deacons crushed the Mustangs 49-7, with 42 points scored in the first half. It was a spanking! Quarterback Gio Lopez accounted for 201 yards and a TD in the air, plus 34 yards and two more TDs on the ground, while the running backs added another 252 yards and four TDs. SMU, which is a good team with a solid record, could do absolutely nothing against these guys. They committed three turnovers and were not able to score until garbage time in the third quarter.

Phillies Sign Max Kranick To Minor League Deal
content:
The Phillies are bringing in right-hander Max Kranick on a minor league deal, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. It’s a non-roster, split contract for the Covenant Sports Group client. The precise salary terms are not clear, though Kranick will presumably earn more than the minor league minimum for any time spent there. Sammon adds that the Phillies will give Kranick a chance to work as a starter.

Kranick, 29, has pitched in parts of four major league seasons from 2021-26. He tossed 43 2/3 innings for the Pirates from 2021-22 before undergoing Tommy John surgery in June of the latter year. He spent 2023-24 recovering, then pitching at Triple-A for the Pirates and Mets’ affiliates. Resurfacing in the Majors in 2025, Kranick had a 3.65 earned run average in 37 innings for the Mets before undergoing flexor tendon surgery that July.

Kranick joined the Nationals organization this past May while he wrapped up his recovery from surgery. He debuted for the team in July but delivered an unsightly 9.33 ERA in 17 appearances. Velocity wasn’t the problem, as Kranick averaged 95.4 mph on his four-seamer, nearly matching his 2025 velocity. Instead, the righty was far too wild on the mound. He surrendered 13 walks in just 18 1/3 innings pitched, and he walked more hitters (13.8%) than he struck out (11.7%). He allowed 27 hits in total, four of which were home runs.

The minor league results have been better, but still not great. Kranick threw 16 2/3 innings across three levels of the Nationals’ system this year and had a 4.32 ERA, along with a so-so 21.1% strikeout rate. In his last full minor league season in 2024, he had a 3.57 ERA in 63 innings for the Mets’ top affiliate, though he coughed up 12 home runs and benefited from an 82.0% strand rate. Kranick was a full-time starter early in his minor league career but has mostly been a reliever since 2024.

The deal is little more than a depth flier for the Phillies. Their rotation is pretty set with Cristopher Sánchez and Zack Wheeler leading the way. Sánchez finished as the NL Cy Young runner-up for the second straight year. Wheeler remains highly effective as the No. 2 guy, and Jesús Luzardo is overqualified as the No. 3 option. Aaron Nola and Andrew Painter round out the group. Bringing on Kranick as depth doesn’t hurt, even if it’s a long shot that he actually sticks as a starter. As the Phillies were reminded at the end of their regular season, injuries can throw an entire rotation off course heading into the playoffs.

The Phillies have one pitching prospect in MLB Pipeline’s Top 100. That prospect is right-hander Gage Wood, a flamethrower who was the team’s first-round draft pick in 2025. He reached the Double-A level in 2026 but struggled with the long ball. He’s no guarantee to make the Majors in 2027. Most of the team’s other pitching prospects are in the lower levels of the minors. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander calls out reporter over AI blunder
content:
Oklahoma City Thunder All-Star guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is the reigning back-to-back NBA MVP.

Gilgeous-Alexander is also now the NBA’s preeminent Anti-AI King.

On Friday, the Thunder suffered a 113-112 loss to the Los Angeles Clippers despite Gilgeous-Alexander dropping 40 points. It was a night to forget for Oklahoma City, until the final question of Gilgeous-Alexander’s postgame press conference created a clip that will live forever.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander fact-checking an LA reporter who used AI search results to get an incorrect stat lmao https://t.co/B4wZbSFv7B

— Clemente Almanza (@CAlmanza1007) November 14, 2026

“Shai, during the first half, it was the first time in your NBA career that you didn’t record a single assist,” an off-camera reporter said. “At what point during the game — I mean, you ended the game with 40 — do you feel like you have to turn that up a notch and start taking over the game offensively?”

“Wait, one more time? It was— wait, what?” Gilgeous-Alexander inquired, peering over his glasses quizzically.

The reporter repeated that Gilgeous-Alexander’s failure to record an assist in the first half against the Clippers marked the first such instance of his decorated career.

“That’s a false stat, by the way,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “In Game 4 against Indiana, I didn’t have an assist the whole game. But sorry. Go ahead.”

It’s true. In Game 4 of the 2025 NBA Finals against the Indiana Pacers, Gilgeous-Alexander posted 35 points, three rebounds, three steals, and one block, but zero assists.

The reporter repeated his actual question, which Gilgeous-Alexander answered. “Gotcha,” the reporter said once Gilgeous-Alexander finished. “Don’t trust AI.”

Gilgeous-Alexander smiled and laughed, saying, “Yeah, don’t do it. Definitely don’t do it!”

Clemente Almanza, lead writer for OKC Thunder Wire, was at the presser and described the reporter only as “an LA reporter.” As of this writing, he has not been identified beyond that, which is probably for the best.

While the predominant lesson here is to never rely on AI for research — or any journalistic function — it also calls back to evergreen advice from the great Kevin Van Valkenburg, formerly of ESPN and now at Fried Egg Golf.

“A great journalism lesson: If you are trying to get good answers from someone in an interview, one of the worst ways to do it is long-ass questions designed to make you (the interviewer) feel or look smart,” Van Valkenburg wrote in May.

title: Mets Among Suitors For Ty France
content:
First baseman Ty France was one of the underrated gems of the 2026 season, batting .295/.363/.502 with a 141 wRC+ for the Padres after entering camp on a non-roster deal. Now, he rates as the No. 23 free agent on MLBTR’s Top 50 list as well as arguably the best first baseman available. Just over a week ago, it was reported that “multiple teams” are showing interest in France. The Mets are one of those suitors, as Mark W. Sanchez of The New York Post reports that New York has touched base with France’s camp as they look to upgrade at first base.

The Mets got terrible production at the cold corner this year, so it’s no surprise they’re exploring all options. First basemen around the league combined for a 114 wRC+ in 2026, with all but six teams getting above-average hitting out of that spot. Unfortunately, the Mets were one of those six clubs. The team ranked second worst with an 85 wRC+ at first base. Only the Diamondbacks (74 wRC+) got less production.

For New York, a lot of that trouble comes down to the regression of Mark Vientos and the injury-driven failure of the Jorge Polanco experiment. Polanco signed a two-year, $40MM deal last December, and the Mets planned to use him at first base and DH. Instead, he hardly played at either spot thanks to a pair of long IL stints for a right wrist contusion and left ankle bursitis, the latter of which required season-ending surgery in August. In the end, Polanco suited up for just 37 games and played all of 20 innings at first base. According to president of baseball operations David Stearns (as relayed by Sanchez), Polanco’s rehab is “going very well,” though the Mets will evaluate him in Spring Training before determining his role.

Vientos, meanwhile, took just under 300 trips to the plate and batted just .212/.258/.394 with a 78 wRC+. The right-handed hitter was a solid platoon option against lefties (119 wRC+) but was unplayable against righties (48 wRC+). Vientos is out of options and a non-tender candidate, so between that and the uncertainty around Polanco following his injuries, the Mets are reportedly seeking a right-handed hitting platoon partner for Jared Young at first base.

France would fit that bill, and he’s not even a pure platoon bat. He posted a 137 wRC+ in 138 plate appearances against lefties but also had a 142 wRC+ in 362 PA against right-handed pitchers. As an added bonus, France is also a good defender, earning +15 and +7 ratings from Defensive Runs Saved and Outs Above Average this year, respectively. That would be a welcome change of pace for the Mets, who in recent years have gotten poor defense from Vientos and Pete Alonso, along with average fielding from Young.

MLBTR projects France for two years and $32MM in free agency. The other top first baseman, Jake Bauers, just went to the Red Sox on a four-year, $58MM deal that exceeded industry expectations. France could feasibly beat industry projections too and might sign a deal before the widely expected lockout. The remaining free agent options aside from France include Paul Goldschmidt, Josh Bell, and Alec Bohm, all of whom are part-time first basemen at best.

title: Texas And LSU Had A Barnburner Of Dumbass Football
content:
The Texas Longhorns triumphed in an exciting, last-second 22-21 victory over the LSU Tigers on Saturday, thanks to a heroic effort by QB Arch Manning and some typical breaking down of the LSU defense. But if you did not watch the contest in full, do not let the thrilling end fool you: This was some of the year's dumbest football, authored by two of our dumbest college football programs.

Let's start with the six interceptions total in this game: three for each, which is nice and neat. At first, it was LSU's Sam Leavitt throwing most of the picks, two in the first half, which makes it particularly strange that LSU was leading for the majority of this game. They were helped by the fact that Manning tossed two picks in the second half, to add to one he threw in the second quarter, and as a result the game was the Tigers' for the taking—21-10 late in the third, and still 21-16 when they punted with only 2:19 to go.

But if nothing else, Manning has shown an ability to get better when his back is against the wall. And if you're going to beat Texas, you have to stomp them out completely. Despite Manning's overall pedestrian performance, 174 yards on 19 of 35 passes, his night climaxed with the crucial touchdown. In the game's final two minutes, Manning led a 12-play, 58-yard drive down the field, culminating in a seven-yard run on third down at LSU's 11-yard line and then a four-yard TD pass to RB Raleek Brown for the go-ahead score. Cue the Texas sideline going absolutely, understandably nuts.

Coach Jackie J implores Netflix to address access for sports bars ahead of women’s World Cup
content:
The 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup figures to be one of the top sports stories of the year, with a more level playing field among the best teams and the USWNT hungry to avenge their early exit in 2023.

The Women’s World Cup will also be an experiment to see whether Netflix can successfully broadcast a big live sports tournament. The streamer has exclusive broadcast rights to the World Cup in the U.S. and Canada. Previously, Fox had the rights to the tournament, making accessibility a pretty easy question to answer — games would be available to watch on Fox and its affiliated channels. Streaming is a bit of a different beast.

Looking ahead to the event, breakout women’s sports personality Coach Jackie J is calling on Netflix to expand access to the games. So far, Netflix has not developed a plan to make the World Cup available in bars, restaurants and other commercial establishments — a common problem as streamers air more sports, and one that could hamper the momentum coming off the World Cup we just had in North America last summer.

“I have heard from owners of sports bars across the country, multiple different people messaging me, saying they’re worried they won’t be able to host any watch parties for one of the biggest women’s sports events of all time,” Coach Jackie said this week on her podcast, Is She Game? “Why? Because Netflix has the sole rights to the Women’s World Cup in 2027, and they’re a subscription service. And that is technically unavailable to commercial establishments. There’s no commercial licensing situation set up right now.”

Technically, it is illegal for bar or restaurant owners to show games through a personal streaming login. Companies like EverPass Media work as intermediaries, striking deals with streamers and then charging restaurant owners to air streaming games legally in their buildings. Some streamers offer standalone subscriptions for businesses. These commercial subscriptions can cost hundreds per month, on top of traditional cable. But businesses can be fined thousands if they show games illegally.

The problem has already cropped up as Prime Video and Peacock bought exclusive rights to big sporting events like NFL playoff games in recent years. Netflix’s ownership of the World Cup will be among the most prominent case studies.

Coach Jackie is calling the problem out early to set a precedent that Netflix ought to be a good partner for a growing women’s sports property.

“You want people to watch this, I want people to watch your broadcast … but if the bars and the places where people come together, can’t watch it, then it’s not going to hit the mark,” she said.

“Think about it, if the women’s sports bars who care the most about this, are the most proactive in figuring out how to get it on TV, if they’re not able to get it on TV, you think the normie bars are going to be pulling it up on Netflix in their bar? No.

“Netflix needs to make it super accessible, and they need to make sure that if they do put out a commercial licensing fee, they need to make sure it’s not a bajillion dollars. Because women’s sports, we’ve already got a lot going on for us right now, we do not need an extra barrier to entry for the best tournament in sports.”

Women’s sports bars are seen as a key source of growth for the WNBA and other leagues. Businesses like the Sports Bra in Portland have built strong communities around airing women’s sports and hosting watch parties.

If Netflix wants to get in on more World Cup rights or larger NFL packages in the future, it must prove to its league partners and fans that its broadcasts will be accessible just as widely and easily as other sports can be found on Fox, CBS, or ESPN.
