title: Yankees Re-Sign Tim Hill To One-Year Deal
content:
The Yankees are bringing back a known quantity for their bullpen. Left-hander Tim Hill is returning on a one-year, $2.25MM deal, per ESPN’s Jeff Passan. The pact includes a $2.5MM club option for the 2028 season. Hill is a client of Paragon Sports International.

Hill, who will turn 37 in Spring Training, has pitched for the Yankees since midway through the 2024 season. The soft-tossing lefty is primarily a ground ball specialist. He has a 63.2% ground ball rate for his career, and since the start of 2024, over two-thirds of batted balls against Hill have been on the ground. That’s easily the best mark among qualified relievers in that span.

For the first two years of his Yankees tenure, Hill backed that up with solid run prevention. In 111 innings with New York from 2024-25, he delivered a 2.68 earned run average, held opposing hitters to a .604 OPS, and posted a sharp 5.7% walk rate. Hill’s 44.0% hard-hit rate in that time was not great, but thanks to the gaudy ground ball numbers, he did a good job of keeping the ball in the yard. He allowed only ten home runs in that span with New York, a rate of 0.81 homers per nine innings.

This past year was a different story. Hill led qualified relievers once again with a 68.8% ground ball rate, but his ERA shot up to 4.60 in 58 2/3 innings. Crucially, he allowed a dozen home runs, or a career-high rate of 1.84 HR/9. It was a strange mix of poor luck on the homers and good luck on other forms of contact. Opponents batted just .228 on balls in play off Hill, continuing a three-year trend of low BABIP values, and he also ranked in the 66th percentile by barrel rate (just 6.6%).

Under the surface, ERA estimators were split on Hill’s work. His 5.93 FIP suggested he was quite fortunate to post that 4.60 ERA, while his 3.66 SIERA was more favorable and right in line with last year’s 3.70 SIERA. Meanwhile, the bulk of the damage against Hill came from right-handed batters, who put up a .293/.365/.543 slash line against him. Lefties, on the other hand, batted .213 with a .611 OPS against him.

However lucky Hill was (or wasn’t), his ground ball specialty and still-solid numbers against lefties makes this a decent, low-cost reunion for the Yankees. The team was set to lose six big league relievers in free agency. Hill is not on the same level as David Bednar or Paul Blackburn, but he fills a role and comes back at a minimal cost that shouldn’t inhibit the Yankees’ pursuit of those two.

Bednar was given a qualifying offer, which the 32-year-old seems likely to reject in favor of a multi-year deal. MLBTR ranks Bednar at No. 12 on our list of the Top 50 Free Agents and predicts he’ll sign a four-year, $68MM contract. Blackburn should also find a multi-year deal after breaking out with a 1.59 ERA in 85 innings. Aside from those targets, New York is also considering Adrian Morejon, who is the top reliever in this year’s class, as well as a reunion with old friend Jonathan Loaisiga.

title: Did Ole Miss Simply Lack The Grit To Get To Their Game On Time?
content:
On Friday, a nationwide ground stop lasting over four hours led to thousands of flight cancellations and delays from coast to coast. As a result, we're getting some Sunday afternoon college football, with No. 19 Ole Miss playing Oklahoma in Norman because they couldn't arrive on their previous schedule.

Per Ole Miss, who was flying out of Tupelo, about 50 miles from their campus in Oxford, the ground stop began just a few minutes before the team buses were scheduled to leave for the airport, at 4 p.m. Once they learned that the stop would last for hours, the players were allowed to go, and they were called for a team meeting at 8 p.m., just a little before stop was lifted. Still, it was apparently too late for them to salvage their journey that night, and the SEC ultimately pushed the game back a day as a result.

"At that hour, due to the time required to rescreen the party and travel to the Tupelo airport, the crew's duty time would have expired prior to departure," the Ole Miss statement said. "There were no other flight options at that point, and we determined it was too late to put our student-athletes on a bus trip of eight or more hours. In addition, the flight crew's duty time restrictions prevented us from being able to fly out until Saturday afternoon at the earliest."

title: Robert Griffin III, Desmond Howard trade personal insults while arguing over Jeremiah Smith
content:
Desmond Howard and Robert Griffin III can’t stop bickering—nay, writing novel-sized excerpts to each other—on Twitter, and this is precisely why the “I Ain’t Reading All That” meme exists.

It all started when Howard, an analyst on ESPN’s College GameDay, delivered a hot take about Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith while appearing on First Take.

“When you talk about Jeremiah, it’s more than just losing [quarterback] Julian Sayin,” Howard said. “You’ve got to have those moments. In the last two years, give me one game where Jeremiah Smith, the wide receiver at Ohio State, was the difference in a big game in the last two years. This season and last season. Give me that game. As much as he puts up these magnificent numbers and these one-handed catches, I need moments against the top competition that makes me say ‘he was the guy.'”

Howard’s comments quickly made the rounds, especially because Howard won the Heisman while starring at Michigan in 1991, and Robert Griffin III emerged as Jeremiah Smith’s biggest fan—or Howard’s biggest hater, depending on how you look at it.

While serving as an analyst on Fox’s Big Noon Saturday broadcast of Ohio State’s 28-19 win over Northwestern on Saturday, Griffin addressed Howard’s criticism of Smith.

“When you talk about the Heisman Trophy, my guy Desmond Howard, he’s been very critical of Jeremiah Smith and said, ‘When does this guy ever show up in big-time games?'” Griffin said. “Well, he’s shown up in big-time games all over the place, and Desmond Howard has to stop hating on Jeremiah Smith just because he goes to Ohio State. That’s not the right way to do this, and we’ve got to be better in our Heisman brotherhood.”

Griffin, who won the Heisman as the Baylor quarterback before briefly starring in the NFL, then posted that clip alongside 353 additional words on X (formerly Twitter):

If Ohio State wins out, Jeremiah Smith should win the Heisman Trophy.

He is the best player in the country.

But I also need to address something.

Buckle up, I got time today.

My Heisman brother @DesmondHoward said that Jeremiah Smith has never been the difference in any big games for Ohio State over the past 2 years in an attempt to discredit this young Superstar just because he goes to Ohio State.

It has been determined that his statement is a lie.

But here is the truth.

Jeremiah Smith has more receiving yards, TDS, and catches in his career than Desmond Howard.

Jeremiah Smith is a National Champion. Desmond Howard is not.

THIS YEAR, Jeremiah Smith had 8 catches for 164 yards against #4 Texas in a loss and was unstoppable against #14 Iowa with 11 catches for 206 yards in a win.

Why would Desmond specify the last 2 years?

Because when Jeremiah Smith was a FRESHMAN he went for:

-6 catches for 103 yards 2 TDs to beat #9 Tennessee in the CFP

-7 catches for 187 yards 2 TDs to beat #1 Oregon in the CFP

-5 catches for 88 yards 1 TD to beat #7 Notre Dame with the game sealing 3rd down conversion to win a National Championship.

Jeremiah Smith is the Big Ten all-time leader in receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and tied for first in 100 yard games with 17.

Jeremiah Smith is the FBS record holder for receiving yards for a player in his first 3 years in college.

You see Desmond Howard and anyone with eyes knows that Jeremiah Smith is ALWAYS THE DIFFERENCE on any field he steps on.

Jeremiah Smith is the best player in the Country, one of the greatest WRs we HAVE EVER SEEN in College Football History and an incredible young man who ALWAYS SHOWS UP.

The Heisman fraternity would be honored to welcome him into our family.

Desmond Howard is a legend, but even legends have to be checked. He needs to stop hating on Jeremiah Smith and recognize his greatness regardless of what school he went to.

— Robert Griffin III (@RGIII) November 14, 2026

Howard responded later Saturday night.

“Oh Robert, are you STILL on this app manufacturing Twitter beef for attention?” Howard wrote. “I thought you would have stopped doing that based on how it has worked out for you in the past. Oh well.

“Jeremiah Smith is an extraordinary talent. Nobody is questioning that. My point was whether he’s been THE difference-maker in Ohio State’s biggest games as a Heisman candidate. That’s a legitimate football discussion, not an attempt to discredit the young man based on the school he attends.

“If you’re going to challenge my football opinion, challenge the argument. Don’t manufacture a personal beef with me to get virtual slaps on the back. Great players deserve honest analysis, not automatic praise.

“If you have anything else to say, you can holster those Twitter fingers and find me IRL. I don’t get down with this goofy sh*t. Brother.”

Oh Robert, are you STILL on this app manufacturing Twitter beef for attention? I thought you would have stopped doing that based on how it has worked out for you in the past. Oh well.

Jeremiah Smith is an extraordinary talent. Nobody is questioning that. My point was whether he’s been THE difference-maker in Ohio State’s biggest games as a Heisman candidate. That’s a legitimate football discussion, not an attempt to discredit the young man based on the school he attends.

If you’re going to challenge my football opinion, challenge the argument. Don’t manufacture a personal beef with me to get virtual slaps on the back. Great players deserve honest analysis, not automatic praise.

If you have anything else to say, you can holster those Twitter fingers and find me IRL. I don’t get down with this goofy shit.

Brother.

— Desmond Howard (@DesmondHoward) November 15, 2026

Griffin did not heed Howard’s advice and doubled down on insulting Howard personally in yet another extremely long X post.

Brother Desmond,

I didn’t challenge your opinion.
I destroyed it.

The problem is you are never being honest.

Not honest when it comes to Jeremiah Smith and don’t you think we forgot about CJ Stroud.

It’s all fun and games in a rivalry until you start letting it make you do and say things to influence or prevent a young man at your rival school from winning national awards.

One of your points to argue against Jeremiah Smith was that Jesse Legree from Oregon State was leading the country in receiving yards.

Well, you didn’t lead the country in receiving yards in your Heisman worthy year.

So should Aaron Turner of the Pacific Tigers having 1,601 yards receiving to your 950 receiving yards have prevented you from winning the Heisman? Is that an honest football conversation?

No. Its ridiculous.

Put the hatred you have for Ohio State aside when it comes to swaying the public away from appreciating the greatness in front of them.

You are better than that.
If you aren’t, than WE AS HEISMAN’S are better than that.

Great players deserve honest analysis, not biased takedown attempts or fabricated analysis to stick it to your rival.

Hold this L.

— Robert Griffin III (@RGIII) November 15, 2026

“Brother Desmond, I didn’t challenge your opinion. I destroyed it. The problem is you are never being honest,” Griffin wrote.

After running through some more pro-Smith talking points, Griffin added:

“Put the hatred you have for Ohio State aside when it comes to swaying the public away from appreciating the greatness in front of them. You are better than that. If you aren’t, than WE AS HEISMAN’S are better than that.

“Great players deserve honest analysis, not biased takedown attempts or fabricated analysis to stick it to your rival.

If that weren’t enough, Griffin punctuated his post by photoshopping himself dunking over Howard.

Perhaps the most amusing part of this nonsense is that it’s probably moot. Smith is favored to win the Heisman, with 1,317 yards and 15 receiving touchdowns. Smith is second only to Oregon State’s Jesse Legree in receiving yards and tied with Legree for the most receiving touchdowns in the nation. And even if Miami quarterback

title: Phillies Interested In Jonathan Loaisiga
content:
Reports indicate that right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga is receiving widespread interest in free agency. The Dodgers were the most recent entrant into his market alongside the Yankees, Mets, and Blue Jays. It appears the Phillies have also entered the fray for Loaisiga’s services, as reported by Jon Heyman of the New York Post. That makes at least five known suitors for the 32-year-old reliever, whom MLBTR projects to earn a two-year, $13MM deal.

Loaisiga is coming off his best season in five years. Despite having a length injury history, including IL stints in every season from 2019-25, he finally stayed off the IL in 2026 and delivered 67 innings out of the Diamondbacks’ bullpen. That was a nice surprise considering Loaisiga entered Spring Training as a non-roster invitee. Even better, he delivered a stellar 2.42 earned run average, 56.4% ground ball rate, and 5.0% walk rate, making him one of Arizona’s best relievers and a key upside play for bullpen-needy clubs in free agency.

That Loaisiga managed a 67-inning total is impressive considering he combined for just 51 1/3 innings from 2023-25 with the Yankees. Since breaking out with a 2.17 ERA in 70 2/3 innings back in 2021, Loaisiga had missed time for shoulder inflammation, elbow inflammation, a torn UCL (which required season-ending surgery in April 2024), and mid-back tightness. From 2022-25, he had a 3.81 ERA in just under 100 innings with a subpar 9.4% K-BB rate but an excellent 55.5% ground ball rate.

There were a lot of positives in Loaisiga’s performance this year beyond the improved health. After working with slightly diminished velocity on his trademark sinker in 2025, he bumped it back up to 97.9 mph with the D-backs, which was right in line with his career norms. According to Statcast, Loaisiga ranked in the 92nd percentile or better by hard-hit rate (31.7%), chase rate (35.9%), barrel rate (3.5%), and average exit velocity (85.2 mph). Every one of his pitches had a positive run value, led by the four-seamer at +10 RV.

The Phillies ranked eighth in the Majors with 5.6 fWAR out of their relievers this year. Most of that came from flamethrowing closer Jhoan Duran, who earned 2.9 fWAR with a career-best 1.82 ERA and 31.4% K-BB rate in 61 appearances. Tim Mayza and Jonathan Bowlan were solid, but José Alvarado, Orion Kerkering, and Chase Shugart posted subpar run prevention and ground ball rates.

Loaisiga would solve both problems on a relatively inexpensive deal. As MLBTR’s Leo Morgenstern noted in our Offseason Outlook series, the Phillies could probably use three relievers but may focus more on bolstering the lineup, especially by adding starting-caliber outfielders. Our Payroll Tracker has the team at a $265MM cash payroll for 2027, leaving around $26.8MM to spend before they match last year’s total.

title: Pat McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit apologize to Wake Forest: ‘I don’t know what we were thinking’
content:
It only took one half of football for Pat McAfee and Kirk Herbstreit to admit they made a poor choice with their Wake Forest-SMU picks on College GameDay.

During Saturday’s edition of College GameDay in Boise, the ESPN college football analysts each picked SMU to beat No. 13 Wake Forest in Dallas.

https://t.co/AHZT24xpx3

— The Comeback NCAA (@TheComebackNCAA) November 15, 2026

“I don’t want to be one of those naysayers, and I love Coach Dickert, and I like Wake Forest,” McAfee said before turning the game prediction into a quick promo for College GameDay sponsor Coors Light.

“I’m going to watch SMU win this game,” McAfee added. “They are not ranked, but I like the SMU Mustangs to steal one here.”

Herbstreit then explained why he liked SMU to win the game.

“I said at the beginning of the show; Pat and I talked about this; it was like a chaos Saturday,” Herbstreit said. “I think there’s a lot of upsets up in the top-25. This is a great Wake Forest team. Thing is, SMU, since they joined the ACC, 12-0 at home in conference games. If you watched them last week, they put up 51 points. I just think they’re playing great football. Kevin Jennings, the difference in today’s game. They outscore Wake. And they’ll be ranked, finally, next week.”

Well, then the game started at 12 p.m. ET, and by halftime, Wake Forest had a 42-0 lead. The Demon Deacons would go on to win 49-7.

Fewer than two hours after College GameDay concluded, McAfee and Herbstreit delivered an apology to Wake Forest in a video posted to Herbstreit’s X account.

Herbstreit posted the following caption: “Whelp. Both [McAfee] and I want apologize from the bottom of our hearts for picking against [Wake Forest]. We thought SMU at home had a chance and BOY WE WE WRONG!! These boys are for real! Congrats and WE BELIEVE!”

Whelp. Both @PatMcAfeeShow and I want apologize from the bottom of our hearts for picking against @WakeFB
We thought SMU at home had a chance and BOY WE WE WRONG!!
These boys are for real!
Congrats and WE BELIEVE! https://t.co/CNBfE0X3LL

— Kirk Herbstreit (@KirkHerbstreit) November 14, 2026

“[Jake Dickert] was so good [as a guest on College GameDay] today; we should’ve known,” McAfee said in the video message alongside Herbstreit. “That’s on us.”

“That’s on us,” Herbstreit agreed.

“We apologize to Wake,” McAfee continued. “Wake is real.”

“We love Wake,” Herbstreit added.

“We think they’re so good,” McAfee said. “Like, I don’t know what we were thinking today.”

“What were we thinking?” Herbstreit asked. “I thought, you know, they’re on the road, SMU looked so good last week. I thought, ‘Maybe they’re in a spot to upset Wake.’ Boy, were we wrong.”

“SMU looked good last week,” McAfee responded. “You know who else did? Wake. Wake has looked good every week. We are sorry. That’s on us.”

“We’re sorry. We love Wake… We all love Wake,” Herbstreit reiterated.

Wake Forest improved to 9-1 with the blowout win and made an excellent case to move up in the next College Football Playoff rankings.

title: The Opener: Wilson, Bullpen Targets, AFL Award Winners
content:
The recently-retired Justin Verlander won his first of three career Cy Young awards on this day in 2011. Verlander fired off a career-high 251 innings in the regular season with a 2.40 earned run average, 250 strikeouts, four complete games, and an impressive 24-5 record. He was so dominant that year that he also won the AL MVP award a few days later, just the tenth time a pitcher won the Cy Young and MVP awards in the same year. Clayton Kershaw would become the eleventh such player in 2014.

1. A’s fielding calls from shortstop-needy teams

The Athletics are reportedly receiving trade interest in shortstop Jacob Wilson. There is no indication that the A’s are seriously looking to move him, so the interest could just be due diligence or fishing for a low-ball offer. Wilson, who underwent season-ending shoulder surgery in September, is entering the second season of a seven-year, $70MM extension inked back in January. In 80 games this year, he put up an 83 wRC+ while playing quality defense, as evidenced by his +9 Outs Above Average and +8 Fielding Run Value. A trade for Wilson would certainly be out of the box, though the interest is not surprising considering the state of the shortstop market in free agency. In MLBTR’s Top 50 Free Agents list, only Mauricio Dubón and J.P. Crawford are options at short, and they’re multi-positional types.

2. Dodgers, Yankees seeking bullpen upgrades

Big surprise. Almost every team is looking for quality relievers, and the Dodgers and Yankees are no different. The Dodgers are reportedly looking at Jonathan Loaisiga and Tim Hill. Loaisiga, who is coming off an excellent season for the Diamondbacks, is drawing interest from at least four teams and “getting closer” to signing a deal. At least five teams have known interest in Hill. As for the Yankees, general manager Brian Cashman calls upgrading the bullpen his “main priority” for the offseason. If they don’t manage to re-sign David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, and/or Hill, it’s possible the team could make a run at Adrian Morejon.

3. Arizona Fall League announces 2026 award winners

The Arizona Fall League just had its championship game yesterday, and with that, the league announced its award winners for the 2026 season. Among that group is Nationals pitching prospect Jarlin Susana, who won Pitcher of the Year. The 22-year-old right-hander was acquired from the Padres in the Juan Soto blockbuster back in August 2022. Susana reached Triple-A for the first time this year and currently rates as the No. 66 prospect in baseball, according to MLB Pipeline. He’s not on the Nats’ 40-man roster but could possibly debut for them in 2027.

title: Oklahoma AD Roger Denny fires back at SEC ‘carnival barker’ Paul Finebaum
content:
Along with disrupting travel nationwide, the FAA-issued ground stop has led to Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny and ESPN college football analyst Paul Finebaum trading barbs.

On Friday night, Denny released a statement blasting the decision made by Commissioner Greg Sankey and the SEC to move Oklahoma’s game vs. Ole Miss from Saturday to Sunday due to travel issues for Ole Miss.

https://t.co/6z039iPC1m

— Roger Denny (@Oklahoma_AD) November 14, 2026

And on Saturday morning’s edition of SEC Nation on SEC Network, Finebaum went off about Denny’s statement and defended the SEC and Ole Miss. Finebaum said that Denny was “pathetically pandering” to Oklahoma fans.

Paul Finebaum: “I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss… What I don’t think is correct is [Oklahoma AD Roger Denny] pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever…” https://t.co/k124Yv7Ocq

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 14, 2026

“I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss. But I believe the administration and Ole Miss did everything they could,” Finebaum said. “What I don’t think is correct is Roger Denny, the athletic director there, pathetically pandering to his fanbase at midnight to try to cover up whatever, I don’t know.”

“Mr. Denny, the commissioner of the Southeastern Conference made a decision for the entire conference and for the safety of everyone,” Finebaum added. “He’s not concerned about what you’re doing with your fanbase. And what Roger Denny has been doing all this year is pandering to his fanbase.”

Well, later on Saturday, Denny responded to Finebaum’s comments during an in-studio appearance on On3’s Sooner Scoop.

Denny was asked, “Do you think this hurt [Oklahoma’s] relationship with [the SEC?]?”

He proceeded to refer to Finebaum as the SEC’s “carnival barker.”

Oklahoma AD Roger Denny went on with the @SoonerScoop crew and did not hold back. https://t.co/zJPQBgAzW4

— Andy Staples (@AndyStaples) November 14, 2026

“I don’t know. They’ll probably send their carnival barker out there to accuse me of pandering again,” Denny said. “And candidly, I don’t care. My job and my duty is to our players, our university, and our fanbase. If they don’t like the way we handle their business, I just don’t much care about that.”

And you can be sure that Finebaum, ESPN’s voice on all things SEC, will have a response to those comments in the coming days.

The Ole Miss-Oklahoma game was originally scheduled to kick off at 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday but was moved to 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. It will be televised on SEC Network, fittingly.

The post Oklahoma AD Roger Denny fires back at SEC ‘carnival barker’ Paul Finebaum appeared first on Awful Announcing.

title: How to Watch Patriots vs. Lions: TV Channel, Live Stream, Time
content:
The New England Patriots face the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. ET from Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

The Lions are 6-2 and take a four-game winning streak to Munich, the last three by 10 points or fewer, including a win at Miami in Week 9. They sit a half game behind Chicago in the NFC North. The Patriots are 5-4 after a home loss to Green Bay and trail Buffalo by two and a half games in the AFC East.

Below are the details on how to watch.

Drake Maye ranks sixth in the NFL with 2,282 passing yards, but he has also thrown 11 interceptions. Three of them came in the loss to Green Bay on Nov. 8, a game in which he also threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns.

He has been sacked 20 times, and Detroit has 27 sacks, third-most in the NFL. That pass rush is the risk, but his 8.4 yards per attempt gives him a way through a Lions defense that allows 260.9 passing yards per game, the most in the NFL.

Only two interceptions all season, along with 15 touchdown passes, give Goff a 106.4 QBR for a 6-2 Lions team. His 2,134 passing yards rank ninth in the NFL, though he managed only 170 yards and one interception at Miami on Nov. 8.

New England allows 231.9 passing yards per game, the eighth-most in the NFL, and has 25 sacks to Goff's 19 taken. His two interceptions meet a Patriots defense with five of its own in nine games, so New England has to force mistakes he rarely makes.

Four 100-yard games and nine rushing touchdowns have Gibbs third in the NFL with 847 rushing yards. He ran for 153 yards and a score against Minnesota on Nov. 1, then got 74 yards on 20 carries at Miami on Nov. 8.

He averages 4.8 yards per carry, down from the 6.7 he posted against the Vikings, and Detroit runs for 127.8 yards per game as a team. His 105.9 rushing yards per game run into a Patriots defense that allows 96.7 per game, ninth-fewest in the NFL.

title: Latest On Ketel Marte
content:
Diamondbacks officials met with  Ketel Marte’s agent Charisse Espinosa-Dash during the GM Meetings this week, but the D’Backs “but did not seem to come away with a clear idea about what teams to which Marte would be willing to approve a deal,” the Arizona Republic’s Nick Piecoro writes.  Marte has full no-trade protection as a 10-and-5 player, so even though he is one of the offseason’s most prominent trade candidates, the possibility exists that Marte will remain in Arizona simply because he isn’t interested in changing teams.

It puts the D’Backs in something of an awkward position, especially since the impending lockout will interrupt all transactions activity for what could be months on end.  If Marte isn’t dealt by 10:59pm CT on December 1 (when the current collective bargaining agreement expires and the league is expected to lock out the players), the uncertainty over his future will continue to linger over all of the Diamondbacks’ remaining offseason plans.

As Piecoro puts it, “the Diamondbacks seem to have little choice but to sort of blindly attempt to make the best deal possible without knowing whether Marte will approve it.”  In terms of what that best deal might entail, Piecoro writes that the D’Backs have looked into all variety of trades in their early discussions about Marte — bringing in just prospects, swapping the second baseman for other established big league talents, or a trade package of both veteran and younger talent.

GM Mike Hazen naturally didn’t go into any detail about the Marte negotiations, but the executive expressed some regret at focusing on MLB-ready younger players in past trades of such star players as Zack Greinke or Paul Goldschmidt.  This could hint that Hazen is looking to add just the best talent available (whether that’s current big leaguers or longer-term prospects) while shopping Marte, which is probably a logical approach since Hazen’s options are already limited by Marte’s no-trade leverage.

One option still under consideration is moving Marte for another player on a hefty contract, for salary offset purposes.  The Diamondbacks “did not seem to be leaning in that direction,” as Piecoro says that Arizona’s preference would be to clear some of Marte’s remaining $91.75MM salary off the books and then reinvest that money into other roster needs.  That $91.75MM figure is a little higher than the $87.5MM owed to Marte in the initial terms of his contract, as Piecoro hears from a source that Marte unlocked incentive bonuses based on plate appearances.

The Blue Jays, Giants, Mariners, Phillies, Pirates, Rays, Red Sox, and Tigers all reportedly had some level of interest in Marte last offseason, and Toronto’s interest has continued into this winter.  As MLBTR’s Anthony Franco explored in a recent post about Marte’s potential market, Seattle, San Francisco, and Pittsburgh are probably out of the running based on various factors emerging within the last year.  There’s also the possibility that Marte’s infamous no-show of a game in Boston this past August might have put past suitors or any other teams off entirely.

title: Rex Ryan to appear on ESPN’s ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’ days after arrest
content:
ESPN analyst and former NFL head coach Rex Ryan turned himself in to authorities and was arrested in Nashville on Wednesday after allegedly running over the feet of two pedestrians with his pickup truck and leaving the scene earlier this month.

Just days later, it seems that Ryan will still appear on ESPN’s programming, including Sunday’s edition (10 a.m. ET) of the network’s NFL pregame show, Sunday NFL Countdown.

ESPN released a statement on Saturday night saying, “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.”

From an ESPN spokesperson on Rex Ryan:

“As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.”

Would not expect Ryan to address the matter on air.

— Richard Deitsch (@richarddeitsch) November 15, 2026

According to Nashville police, the pedestrians were crossing Broadway Street with a walk sign when Ryan turned right before “running over both victims’ feet,” along with “making contact with one of the individuals’ legs.”

Ryan allegedly kept driving, but the victims caught up to him at a red light. “They said he stepped out of the truck to argue with them, got back in, and drove away,” per the police statement.

The former head coach of the New York Jets (2009-14) and Buffalo Bills (2015-16) faces six misdemeanors: two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information/render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal.

After the news of Ryan’s arrest emerged on Wednesday, ESPN issued the following statement when reached by Awful Announcing for comment: “We are aware and are in touch with Rex.”

Ryan, 63, has been an analyst on ESPN since 2017 and stars on Sunday NFL Countdown alongside Mike Greenberg, Randy Moss, Alex Smith, Tedy Bruschi, and Adam Schefter. He’s also a frequent guest on ESPN’s Get Up.

Update: Rex Ryan indeed appeared on Sunday’s edition of Sunday NFL Countdown on ESPN.

title: Jason Garrett pays heartfelt tribute to Dan Hicks on NBC’s Notre Dame broadcast
content:
The sports media world suffered a devastating loss with the sudden passing of beloved broadcaster Dan Hicks this week at the age of 64. Hicks delivered a remarkable career as a play-by-play broadcaster, headlined by 35 years as a versatile voice for NBC Sports, which included iconic calls in golf and the Olympics.

Additionally, Hicks was NBC’s voice of Notre Dame football from 2014 to 2016 and took over in the prestigious role again in 2024. And in that second stint, Hicks spent the three seasons working alongside Jason Garrett in the NBC booth.

Hicks and Garrett were scheduled to work together again for Saturday’s Notre Dame game against Boston College until the tragic news of Hicks’ death from an acute illness. Jason Benetti stepped in to call the game for NBC and did a beautiful job paying tribute to Hicks throughout the day.

In the moments ahead of kickoff, Benetti delivered an emotional message about being in the booth.

“A campus that was so full of joy this week; our broadcast booth feels very hollow right now here at NBC Sports,” Benetti said. “Our colleague of 35 years, Dan Hicks, passed away on Wednesday. I wish I wasn’t here right now. Jason Benetti, Jason Garrett. I wish Dan was here right now. And I know everybody does.”

“I know how close you and he were, Jason,” Benetti said to Garrett.

Garrett then opened up on the friendship he had with Hicks and explained what a great person Hicks was beyond the broadcasting accolades.

Jason Garrett reflects on his friendship with Dan Hicks, sharing the memories and lasting impact that will stay with him forever. https://t.co/CoKKwPfBmD

— NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 14, 2026

“You know, Hicksy had some of the most iconic calls in any sporting event in history,” Garrett began. “What I always loved about Hicksy, it never was about him. It was always about embracing the moment and highlighting the people involved. And that’s how he lived his life. As legendary a broadcaster as he was, he was a better guy. Devoted husband, and father, and friend. He was always so generous to me in the booth. I can’t tell you the number of times that he would look over to me and say, ‘How you doing? Do you need anything? Can I tee you up?’ That was his line.”

“He had an amazing spirit,” Garrett continued. “He brightened every room that he went into, and he was so funny. We had so much fun together. He told great stories. And he was a great impersonator. He used to do Tom Brokaw, and [Bob Costas], and John Facenda. We actually had him once do JFK. He called a play doing JFK.

“You know, yesterday, you were with us,” Garrett said to Benetti. “Everybody from NBC went over to the Grotto here at Notre Dame to light a candle and say a prayer for him and his family. And I was walking back, and there was a sign on Notre Dame’s campus that said, ‘What does it mean to live a good life?’ And I thought about Hicksy. You know, brightening people’s lives, and striving each day to make the world a better place. And that’s just who he was. That’s why everybody loved him so much. That’s why these tributes that we’ve all seen over the last few days are just remarkable.”

Garrett proceeded to tell his favorite story about Hicks.

“And I have so many stories of him, but my favorite happened right here,” Garrett explained. “Before every game, Notre Dame is a mecca. People come far and wide to see the Irish play football. We had so many people. It’s like Grand Central Station in this booth every week. Whether it’s family, or friends, or former players coming in here, and invariably, it would be like 15 minutes before the game. We’re just about to get going. Hicksy is knee-deep in his preparation.

“And every single time, he would spin his chair around, and he would welcome the people in. It might be two five-year-old kids with their parents and grandparents. And he would show them his spotting board. He’d go over to the telestrator and let them play with that. And show them the view, or the cameras that we had. And we’d get right here in this very spot. And we’d do this team selfie together. And Hicksy didn’t even know these people, but he was right in the middle, hugging them, and smiling with them.

“It’s just who he was. He just went above and beyond trying to make people’s lives better and their day brighter. It’s just who he was and why we loved him so, so much. One of the greatest privileges of my life is to call him my partner and my friend. And we’re going to miss him very, very much.”

“You know how beautiful it is that you’re smiling when you’re thinking about him, though?” Benetti responded.

“He’s the best,” Garrett said.

title: Sean McVay Gives Injury Updates On Rams Stars Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie
content:
Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett expects to play Sunday despite missing practice, while cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable for their game at the Arizona Cardinals.

Garrett was held out of practice on Friday after being limited earlier in the week because of a knee injury that caused him to miss seven games before returning to make three sacks with a forced fumble in the Rams’ 20-13 win at the Washington Commanders on Sunday.

"He’s had a really good week," coach Sean McVay said. "Played a bunch of snaps, and expect him to be able to build on that. But we’re being smart with him."

Garrett was largely pleased with his performance, in which he played 61.5% of the defensive snaps, apart from needing to build up his endurance and address what he felt was a slow get-off time.

"I'm sure Next Gen or PFF or somebody would tell me it wasn't too bad," Garrett said. "It felt terrible to me."

McDuffie is dealing with a back injury that forced him to miss the Rams’ third straight win last week, getting them over .500 for the first time this season at 5-4. McVay expressed optimism he would be able to play, provided McDuffie felt good coming out of Friday's workout.

"He was rolling, you know, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday," McVay said.

The ongoing issues with the Rams’ two marquee offseason acquisitions are indicative of their larger injury crisis that has threatened a campaign that began with them as Super Bowl betting favorites. Los Angeles is so beat up that star wide receiver Puka Nacua was placed on injured reserve Thursday to free up a roster spot, a reversal from what McVay had indicated earlier in the week when he cited the limited number of IR slots remaining to be able to bring players back later in the season.

"Some things changed where we needed that spot because of all the moving pieces," said McVay, while adding that nothing has changed with the timeline for Nacua’s return from knee and toe injuries.

Safety Kam Curl is questionable with a toe injury, but McVay indicated he is likely to play. The same is expected for the Rams’ banged-up crop of tight ends, Colby Parkinson (ribs), Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique). All three are needed to supplement the passing game with top receivers Nacua, Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) on IR.

Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) and left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) were ruled officially out, as was previously announced.

The Rams were upset by the Cardinals 18-16 on Oct. 18, giving up a last-minute drive which ended with Chad Ryland kicking his sixth field goal as time expired at SoFi Stadium.

Reporting by The Associated Press.

title: Dutch Romp Greece, Germany Cruises In UEFA Nations League Action
content:
The Netherlands routed Greece 7-0 in a statement Nations League victory to stay unbeaten under new coach Xavi, while Jürgen Klopp's Germany cruised to a 3-1 win over Serbia on Friday.

That now sets up a decider between the two big-name coaches for first place in their group.

Tijjani Reijnders scored a hat trick and Jurrien Timber had two goals in a rampant win for the Netherlands.

Beaming and holding up three fingers, Reijnders celebrated a hat trick which came off a series of slick team moves to tear apart the Greek defense in Amsterdam.

Crysencio Summerville got the Netherlands started with a sixth-minute opener before Reijnders scored three in the space of 21 minutes, Timber added two more and Donyell Malen a seventh.

Germany is three points behind Group A2 leader the Netherlands before they play on Monday in Berlin.

The top two in the group advance to the quarterfinals, with head-to-head record as the tiebreaker. The Netherlands, Germany and Greece are all able to qualify. Serbia is last after losing all of its five games.

Goals from Florian Wirtz and debutant Brajan Gruda lifted Germany to its second win in five games with Klopp as coach after a slow start to his tenure.

In driving rain, Germany was ahead after just three minutes when Serbia defender Srdjan Babic turned Germany forward Kai Havertz’s header into his own goal.

It was 2-0 soon after when Wirtz flicked a rebound over goalkeeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, who had parried a shot from Havertz.

Klopp’s experimental squad, with Freiburg winger Derry Scherhant but no place for Barcelona’s Karim Adeyemi, added a third when Leipzig's Gruda dribbled through the center of the Serbian defense to score Germany’s third.

Babic canceled out his earlier own goal by scoring for Serbia on a rebound, but chances of a comeback were ended when Vanja Dragojevic was sent off for a reckless tackle on Joshua Kimmich's ankle.

The 50,000-capacity Rajko Mitic stadium was almost empty because Serbia was supported by only 5,000 accompanied children and teenagers. That's because UEFA was punished the Serbian soccer federation for fans’ offensive behavior in the previous rounds.

Switzerland is playing in the second tier of the Nations League for the first time, but its bid to rejoin Europe's elite stayed on course in a 0-0 draw with Slovenia, its closest rival in Group B1. Scotland won against North Macedonia 2-1.

Reporting by The Associated Press.

title: That Was Fast! Vikings HC Kevin O'Connell Reveals Kirk Cousins Timeline
content:
That didn't take long!

Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed in a press conference on Friday afternoon that recently acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins will start in the team's Week 10 road matchup against the Green Bay Packers (1 p.m. ET on FOX); the Vikings defeated the Packers at home in Week 1, scoring 29 consecutive points to get a 39-22 victory.

"I cannot give him enough credit for coming in here with how he's gone about the week, both him and the coaching staff getting him ready to go, working extremely hard, using all the time we possibly can," O'Connell said of Cousins. "It's been really impressive what he's been able to do with the command and just getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with, but certainly some guys he hasn't.

"And it's been something that everybody's been very, very impressed with, so exciting to start Kirk." 

Of course, Cousins' arrival in Minneapolis marks his second stint with the Vikings, as the four-time Pro Bowler played for the franchise from 2018-23 and for O'Connell from 2022-23. Minnesota acquired the 38-year-old Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday afternoon for a 2027 third-round pick.

Across the nine starts he made for the Raiders this season, Cousins totaled 2,340 passing yards, 20 passing touchdowns, eight interceptions and a 97.1 passer rating, while completing 64.1% of his passes.

After starting the season 0-6, the Vikings have lost back-to-back games. In the second of those two losses, a 23-6 defeat at home on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills, Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz tossed two interceptions, threw for only 81 yards and completed just eight passes.

Wentz was starting in place of Kyler Murray, who's dealing with a hamstring strain and will be inactive Sunday, per O'Connell. The Vikings also have quarterback Max Brosmer, who took over for Wentz late in the fourth quarter on Monday night.

title: NFL Trade Deadline: Who Were Biggest Winners, Losers? League Execs React To Top Deals
content:
NFL trade deadline day didn't spark a ton of fireworks, but plenty of fireworks were shot off in the days and weeks leading up to Tuesday.

Of the deals that were made on deadline day, though, none were bigger than the Minnesota Vikings' decision to reunite with Kirk Cousins. The Vikings gave up a third-round pick to land Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders as their quarterback struggles were clearly holding them back. 

Other moves, like the massive trades the Jacksonville Jaguars made on Monday or the deal the Chicago Bears swung two weeks ago, could define this season's homestretch and postseason. And on the flip side, the Indianapolis Colts and Philadelphia Eagles waved the white flag on the season, securing major draft capital. 

So, what should we make of the biggest trade deadline deals? Who won and lost the trade deadline? We asked those questions to general managers, executives and scouts around the league. Here's what we learned. 

Eric D. Williams: While giving Minnesota props for securing a quality quarterback at the trade deadline, an NFL contract negotiator also questioned the team’s personnel department in evaluating previous quarterback decisions and their fit in head coach Kevin O’Connell’s system.

"It’s crazy how expectations can spiral so quickly," the league source told me. "And I mean this more so in regard to Kyler Murray. Going into the season, the expectation was that Kyler was the high-ceiling QB who could return O’Connell’s offense to prominence. But from a pro scouting standpoint, the Minnesota front office clearly missed. And now they’re without a third-round pick.

"Good for them for cutting their losses and acquiring Cousins, but it’s clear that the Murray signing [while not costing them hardly any money] was a swing and a miss."

The contract negotiator sees Cousins as a clear upgrade, but questioned whether the 38-year-old can stay healthy enough to help lead the Vikings on a deep postseason run, considering his past injury history.

"I’m not going to discredit what Cousins can do for Minnesota," the league source told me. "With how that defense is playing, Cousins’ acquisition could also fall in the ‘shooting our shot’ bucket.

"They just need him to be competent in KOC’s offense. They don’t need him to play hero ball. If he can just run the offense, then they’ll have a chance. But yes, health is a concern."

Another league source told me Daniel Jones would have been a better fit if available, but overall liked the trade.

"I wish they could have picked up Daniel, but I understand their thinking," the league source said. "And if the MNF game had gone well, they would not have done anything."

Ralph Vacchiano: For the most part, this is being viewed as a classic win-win trade, to varying degrees.

For the Vikings, the win is obvious: They found what might be the perfect starting QB for them, and it "only" cost them a third-round pick. 

"I mean, they were desperate," one NFL general manager told me. "They were calling everybody. And they had to do it. [Kyler] Murray and [Carson] Wentz had been terrible. They were going to cost them a real chance at a Super Bowl. I would’ve held out for a second, at least, and I think they would’ve had to pay it. They weren’t coming out of this without a quarterback."

They also got what another NFL executive told me was the "perfect guy for them" — a former Viking who knows Kevin O’Connell’s offense and No. 1 wide receiver Justin Jefferson and won’t need long to get up to speed. 

"If you think about it, it’s kind of a miracle," the executive told me. "The right guy at the right price, and he’s available halfway through the season. What are the odds it works out like that?"

As for the Raiders, the general manager summed up their win like this: "They got a 3 for a guy they were going to bench soon anyway. Maybe they have to turn to Fernando Mendoza (their rookie No. 1 overall pick) a little earlier than they wanted. But it was coming soon anyway. Their future is the kid, not the old man. And now they got a Day 2 pick to help the rebuild, too."

Williams: Both league sources I spoke with about Taylor being on the trade market were not surprised the elite running back stayed in Indianapolis.

"I don’t know why the Colts would have traded Taylor at all unless they received a crazy offer," an NFL agent told me. "A new GM and coach would want him. He is 27 and under contract for two years. He just did an extension, so trading him borders on asinine. The Colts could get going the rest of the way. The schedule is reasonable to do so."

Another league source I talked with believes the Colts are holding Taylor hostage by keeping him on a losing roster that’s tanking the rest of the season.

"People lose sight that the players in the locker room are humans," the league source told me. "With everything over the last two weeks pointing to Taylor moving on and him effectively saying his goodbyes after their last game, it was the absolute wrong thing for them to do by not moving him.

"I’m hoping he comes up with a mysterious injury that puts him on IR for the rest of the season, and then they move him in the offseason. That would be the right thing to do." 

Vacchiano: I thought the Colts made the right decision, but I didn’t find many people who agreed with me. Most of my sources saw the decision as a "surprise," and they believed the Colts were going to take the best offer they had, which was believed to be a second-round pick plus a fourth- or fifth-round pick too.

 "That’s a good deal for a running back," one NFL source told me. "They are in a total rebuild. They sold a bunch of their best players. They have huge questions about their offensive line and quarterback. They’re going to have a new GM soon, and maybe a coach. And they’re holding on to a 27-year-old running back as the centerpiece of their rebuilding? Who does that?"

"Taylor is a great player if he’s on a good team," an AFC scout told me. "The Colts won’t be good again for a while, which makes him dead weight. They should’ve taken the 2-plus, fixed their line, and just replaced him with someone younger." 

"I was shocked," the general manager told me. "Really thought he was gone. I love [Taylor], but I don’t know what they’re thinking. And I wouldn’t be shocked if the new GM tries to trade him in the offseason before free agency starts."

Williams: The Chicago Bears and Jacksonville Jaguars are the biggest winners from the moves they made at this year’s trade deadline, according to league sources I spoke with.

"I think Chicago and Jacksonville benefited the most," a league source told me. "They are clearly shooting their shot for a Super Bowl appearance this year."

The Bears, of course, supercharged their defense with the addition of Defensive Player of the Year candidate Jeffery Simmons. Meanwhile, the Jaguars also addressed their deficiencies on defense by adding safety Jesse Bates, along with defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux.

Chicago and Jacksonville have two of the best offenses in the league, led by Caleb Williams and Trevor Lawrence, respectively. We’ll see if the defensive upgrades push them over the edge to becoming legitimate Super Bowl contenders at the end of the year.

One national scout said the Jaguars could be the biggest winners or biggest losers with their "F’ them picks" approach to trading premium picks for premium players, like the Los Angeles Rams. And that makes sense, with general manager James Gladstone and head coach Liam Coen both having spent time in Los Angeles.

"The Jaguars might be the biggest winner and loser," the scout told me. "They went all in and if they win it all, then it’s a win. Or they could lose! But I like the aggressive approach because I think the race is wide open."

Vacchiano: Three teams kept coming up in my discussions with league sources: The Vikings, Jaguars and the Eagles, though a few did praise the Colts and Bears, too.

The Vikings praise was all about the Kirk Cousins deal. 

"Finding a QB who can be the difference between making the Super Bowl or not is a huge win no matter how you look at it," one NFL executive told me. "And at that price? Wow. I guarantee they would’ve given up more."

The Jaguars earned praise for "going for it all," in the words of one GM. 

"I don’t love all their deals or what they paid," he told me, "but good for them not sitting still. There’s a reason they say ‘Fortune favors the bold’. And they were bold." 

The Jaguars were already loaded on offense, but added Bates, Davis and Godchaux at the deadline. 

"They were already a good defense," an AFC scout told me. "They made it stronger." 

The only question was about the price they paid for Davis, which included sending a first-round pick to the Eagles. Two sources told me that was "Way too steep."

And that’s a big reason why Eagles general manager Howie Roseman was one of the winners. They had already dealt center Cam Jurgens to Baltimore for a second-round pick, and for Davis they got a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick, giving them 10 picks in the first two rounds over the next three drafts. 

"I’m a little surprised they didn’t do more," one general manager told me. "But they did great. They always do."

The Bears, meanwhile, earned praise for acquiring Jeffrey Simmons, whom one scout told me was "the only true difference-making defensive player available." The price was high — two first-round picks. 

"But again," the general manager told me, "Good teams go for it. They don’t sit still."

As for the Colts, despite all the questions about not trading Taylor, they did ship off guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, trading four players on expiring contracts for a third, two fourths, two fifths and a sixth. 

"Those may not seem like huge deals," one league executive told me. "But they add up. Better than letting them walk away for nothing."

Williams: League sources pointed to the Indianapolis Colts as the clear losers here, giving up Quenton Nelson, Josh Downs, DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen in a fire sale before the trade deadline.

The Colts had moved on from general manager Chris Ballard, so interim general manager Ed Dodds orchestrated the moves, with the blessing of owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon. We’ll see if head coach Shane Steichen remains around at season’s end to clean up the mess.

One source told me the Colts should have emptied the tank and moved on from running back Jonathan Taylor.

"Indianapolis is the biggest loser by not moving Taylor and taking the reported second and fifth offered for him," the league source told me.

Vacchiano: No team has taken more of a deserved beating from NFL sources around the trade deadline than the Los Angeles Chargers, who had even let teams know they were standing pat despite being 0-8 and generally a mess. They did make one deal — sending linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos for a fourth- and fifth-round pick. But that was it.

And then, late Wednesday night, that trade fell apart anyway.

"Don’t get me started," an NFL executive told me. "Complete malpractice. They weren’t even willing to listen."

"Dumbest thing I’ve seen in years," another executive told me. "I don’t know what they’re thinking. They like their players? Great. They’re doing a bang-up job for them."

They almost certainly could have gotten something for players like edge rusher Khalil Mack, wide receiver Quentin Johnston and cornerback Donte Jackson, and maybe more. 

"But they’re sleeping," one of the NFL executives told me. "I really think nobody is home."

Another loser: The Washington Commanders. But it wasn’t their fault. They had a lot of interest in defensive tackle Daron Payne, according to sources, including from the New York Giants. But Payne got hurt, ending that. 

"I wonder if they would’ve dealt WR Terry McLaurin before he got hurt, too," the source said. "A lot of people were looking for receivers."

One other loser: The Cincinnati Bengals, "mostly for incompetence," the general manager told me. They had a deal in place with Philadelphia for depth edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie. Then a reporter on social media revealed the move would’ve meant they’d also lose a compensatory third-round pick in the next draft, and the Bengals quickly backed out of the deal.

"Embarrassing," the GM told me. "How did they not know that? There are people in every organization whose job, literally, is to figure that stuff out."

"I guess it’s good they found out before they lost the comp pick," an NFL executive told me. "But that’s a terrible look."

It also didn’t help the Bengals’ cause that the Ebiketie deal was the only one they were apparently considering, despite a struggling defense that is holding them back.

"Nobody ever accused the Bengals of being smart," one source told me.

title: 4 Things Pochettino Must Fix At Manchester United
content:
So there you have it. On Friday, Mauricio Pochettino shed his tears in an emotional press conference ahead of the United States men’s national team’s Concacaf Nations League two-legged quarterfinal series against Haiti, confirming what we all knew. The Argentinian is off to Manchester United with a desire to once again reclaim redemption as the 54-year-old manager – formerly at Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea — feels he has unfinished business in the Premier League.

The job is clear. To help a muddled United in complete disarray, which finds itself in 18th place with eight points from the first 10 league matches. This is the club’s worst start in the top flight in 40 years, of course the arrival of a certain Alex Ferguson. What would follow would be a period of glorious dominance throughout the 1990s and early 2000s, including 2012-2013, when the club won its last Premier League trophy to date, making it a record 20 league titles.  

Funnily enough, that was the year when a bright-eyed and eager Argentinian entered the Premier League to take over Southampton. At the time, there were plenty of question marks over Pochettino’s introduction, notably because most of the English press knew little about the incredible work he had done with La Liga minnows Espanyol, which included an early win over Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona. 

But after Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur, where he guided Spurs to four consecutive top-four finishes, a Champions League final and had it not been for a miraculous Leicester City run, perhaps even a Premier League title, Pochettino earned the respect and friendship of the aforementioned Ferguson, who perhaps knew something we didn’t. This was a manager who could one day take over Man United. In fact, with Fergie three years out of management and Pochettino at Tottenham (second season where Spurs ended third), they were publicly spotted having lunch in Mayfair in London back in 2016 – thus enforcing the belief of their deep respect for each other.

How could you not like Pochettino? As a person, much like his mentor Marcelo Bielsa, he is brutally honest, direct and only demands an absolute hunger for the game, no matter your title or reputation. But Pochettino has something Bielsa never mastered, which is charisma. And it’s this charisma that must collectively work with his football on the pitch to resuscitate Man United.

So as Pochettino becomes the first ever South American to take over the Red Devils as head coach, I see this situation with the club very much as the football version of "Mary Poppins." First we have the Man United fanbase, playing the role of the children, Jane and Michael Banks. All they want is love, attention and someone to care for their club. The Glazer ownership, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS — acting very much like George Banks — begrudgingly have hired once again someone who can fix this mess. 

Enter Mary Poppins. Mauricio Pochettino. The internal and external problems are as long as Jane and Michael’s list, but the hope is for their new manager to create magic and help them climb out of this conundrum. 

It will, however, take more than Dick Van Dyke to save this mess, but I think Mar—I mean, Pochettino – is up to the task. 

Here’s what Mauricio Pochettino needs to fix immediately. 
 

It is a clear affirmation that the anger that stems from Man United is not on the head coach. It is on the ownership. We as analysts and pundits have talked about this endlessly and it’s extremely clear that there is a detached, hierarchical, strategic problem within the club. But the Glazer ownership, INEOS—they’re not going anywhere in the near future. 

Pochettino’s arrival, despite being a band-aid over a gunshot wound, needs to be about mending a broken relationship. I’ll get to the tactical outlook on the pitch in a moment, but the overall objective is for the Argentinian to arrive at Carrington and begin to set a precedent of trust between himself, the players, stakeholders and most importantly, the fanbase. He needs them on his side from the very first minute. 

The best way to do that is to speak to the press with honesty, to initiate a culture of blue-collar, hard-work effort on the training pitch, and to speak to the fans, about the fans, with the fans as much as possible. 

This is a Pochettino speciality. He connects with people better than most head coaches and it’s his job from day one, to place the first brick towards the bridge of trust and mutual respect. 

The late legendary basketball coach John Wooden would always say, "nothing will work unless you do," and I think that needs to be graffitied at the training facility in Carrington. Pochettino is known for his detailed -focused routines and gargantuan demands in training, but it all begins with accountability. 

He is a student of Bielsa and no one asks more of you as a person or athlete than the man whose nicknamed is "Loco." Pochettino is the same. And I think United’s number one responsibility is to heighten every asset of training. From eating habits to where you sit at lunch or how you warm up. Pochettino will demand perfection in practice, meaning that a few players will probably get a wake-up call when he arrives next Wednesday. 

What if I told you that the only teams in the Premier League who have conceded more goals are Ipswich Town and manager-less, bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace? United has given up 19 goals, which is just too much after 10 matches. 

Their defensive unit is in peril, and it’s not just about the individual, it’s a collective responsibility that lives within the midfield too. 

Pochettino, therefore, has to find a way to make United stronger at the back, beginning with a daunting trip to Anfield a week on Sunday. 

This isn’t a Pochettino strength per se, as his focus is high pressure and fluidity in the final third. But this has to be a major task for the Argentinian.

As I mentioned before, the mental issues with United are obvious, and it’s important to instill belief into the squad. I think about 21-year-old defender Lenny Yoro, for example, who desperately needs guidance. Or the obvious one, Kobbie Mainoo. He is such a talented midfielder, but what he has needed most is a proverbial arm around his shoulder. 

Pochettino has a fantastic history of developing and nurturing young players. England striker Harry Kane – who became a Tottnham legend under Pochettino's guidance – has alluded to this. Cavan Sullivan, the teenage U.S. star, constantly speaks about Pochettino’s belief in the young Philadelphia Union attacker. Younger members of United, therefore, need Pochettino more than ever. 

But I also think the veterans need it too, beginning of course with midfielder Bruno Fernandes and centerback Harry Maguire. It’s imperative for Pochettino to replace doubt with strength, and finger-pointing with accountability. 

I believe Pochettino can help this squad because this isn’t the same manager who left Chelsea in 2024. The Argentinian found a new version of himself with the U.S. and I’d like to think he arrives at Man United, not as a savior, but a warrior, who can help these down-and-out players pick themselves up again. 

Or, in retrospect, as Mary Poppins flying down from the skies with a magical umbrella, ready to save — not London — but the west side of Manchester.

title: Mauricio Pochettino Leaves The USMNT For An Even Bigger Mess
content:
After an extended denouement to a doomed tenure, Manchester United finally set manager Michael Carrick loose on Thursday, hoping to put an end to the club's worst league start in 40 years. On Friday, the next era for England's most famous club began, sort of, as United announced that Mauricio Pochettino would be leaving the U.S. men's national team on Nov. 18 in order to become the new boss at Old Trafford.

Carrick's departure is no surprise, but Pochettino's arrival counts as a bit of a shock. Pochettino had famously come to international prominence first at Southampton and then in his five-season-plus stint at Tottenham Hotspur, which saw that club's evolution from an also-ran into, well, an also-ran that could actually fight with the big boys. Eventually, his tenure there grew stale and the lack of trophies forced a move, with Tottenham firing him in November of 2019. The Argentine then took a year off before signing on to succeed Thomas Tuchel at Paris Saint-Germain in early 2021; his first half-season there wasn't great, as he oversaw the only PSG squad to not win the Ligue 1 title this decade. He did go on to win the league in his first full season, but PSG let him go in the summer of 2022 anyway. A return to the Premier League with Chelsea followed in 2023, where he finished in sixth place in his only season at Stamford Bridge.

That brings us to September 2024, when Pochettino became manager of the USMNT ahead of the 2026 World Cup cycle. His appointment was a big deal, as he became the highest-paid and most accomplished manager in the country's history (Jurgen Klinsmann will quibble with the latter assessment, but whatever) in advance of a home(-ish) World Cup. Pochettino had a rocky start there, but eventually righted the ship enough to guide the USMNT to a Group D first-place finish and a Round of 32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. An embarrassing loss to Belgium in the Round of 16 put a bit of a damper on the run, but overall, Pochettino did what he was hired to do: help the USMNT perform at the World Cup.

title: Would You Get Stoned With The Scythians?
content:
It's just like they told you it would happen in D.A.R.E.: You have been miraculously, tragically transported 2,800 years back in time, in the land that is now the Uyuk Valley of southern Siberia. The site will be eventually called Tunnug 1 by the archaeologists who excavate it in 2017. But that is the future, and this is the present, meaning 800 B.C. You have come to sit with the Scythians, nomads who roamed the Eurasian steppes on horseback. You have even glimpsed their warrior-king, whose long and stately braids make him seem like a pretty cool guy. Also, he's smoking. Suddenly the warrior-king glimpses you back, his reddish eyes glinting in the firelight. He leans over to you, whispers something inscrutable in an Eastern Iranic language, and extends in his grizzled hands an ancient joint, leaving you with only one question: Would you smoke that shit?

There are, to be certain, pros and cons. But one thing is clear, per a paper published recently in the journal Science: The Scythians were definitely using cannabis to get high. The analysis, led by Fabio-haired University of Bern archaeologist Gino Caspari, represents the earliest definitive evidence of humans consuming marijuana as a psychoactive drug, which was previously only traced back 2,500 years ago where Sogdian mourners once lit up in the ancient Jirzankal Cemetery in what is now western China.

It's only fitting that marijuana hails from one of the highest places in the world: the eastern Tibetan Plateau, also known as the Roof of the World. The plant evolved around 28 million years ago, and as early as 4,000 years ago Chinese farmers cultivated the plant for rope, clothing, and paper, per Science. But it is harder to tell when in the archaeological record ancient people first became gone off that loud. Wild weed, the ancestors of the domesticated kind, has only a little tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC, the plant's intoxicating compound. Some researchers confirmed this when they tried to smoke wild weed and felt nothing, also per Science. (It is unclear if these particular researchers are also the paper's authors, who described cannabis as an "illicit" substance.)
